sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第091卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 91
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 91

sentences.zh: 【晉紀十三】 起屠維單閼，盡重光大荒落，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Jin Records 13] Beginning at Tuxi Danque, ending at Chongguang Dahuangluo, altogether three years.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Records 13] This record runs from the year Tuxi Danque through Chongguang Dahuangluo—a span of three years.

sentences.zh: 中宗元皇帝中太興二年（

translations.literal: Second year of Taixing in the middle reign of Emperor Yuan of the Zhongzong line (
translations.idiomatic: The second year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan of Jin (

sentences.zh: 己卯，公元三一九年）

translations.literal: jimao, the year 319 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jimao, 319 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，劉遐、徐龕擊周撫於寒山，破斬之。

translations.literal: Spring, second month: Liu Xia and Xu Kan attacked Zhou Fu at Han Mountain, defeated him, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the second month, Liu Xia and Xu Kan attacked Zhou Fu at Han Mountain, routed his forces, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 初，掖人蘇峻帥鄉里數千家結壘以自保，遠近多附之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Su Jun of Ye led several thousand households of his home district in building fortifications to protect themselves, and many from near and far attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Su Jun of Ye had rallied several thousand local households behind fortified camps for self-defense, and people from far and wide flocked to his banner.

sentences.zh: 曹嶷惡其強，將攻之，峻帥眾浮海來奔。

translations.literal: Cao Ni resented his strength and was about to attack him; Jun led his followers across the sea to come and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ni, alarmed by his growing power, prepared to attack him, so Jun took his followers by sea and came over to the Jin court.

sentences.zh: 帝以峻為鷹揚將軍，助劉遐討周撫，有功；

translations.literal: The Emperor appointed Jun General Who Displays the Hawk, and in assisting Liu Xia against Zhou Fu he rendered merit;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Jun General Who Displays the Hawk; he aided Liu Xia against Zhou Fu and distinguished himself in the campaign;

sentences.zh: 詔以遐為臨淮太守，峻為淮陵內史。

translations.literal: an edict made Xia Administrator of Linhuai and Jun Interior Minister of Huailing.
translations.idiomatic: and an edict appointed Xia Administrator of Linhuai and Jun Interior Minister of Huailing.

sentences.zh: 石勒遣左長史王修獻捷於漢，漢主曜遣兼司徒郭汜授勒太宰、領大將軍，進爵趙王，加殊禮，出警入蹕，如曹公輔漢故事；

translations.literal: Shi Le sent his Left Chief Clerk Wang Xiu to present a victory report to Han; the Han ruler Liu Yao sent Acting Minister of Works Guo Si to invest Le as Grand Preceptor and Commander-in-Chief, advance his rank to King of Zhao, grant extraordinary honors, and accord him the escort of clearing the road on exit and entry, following the precedent of Duke Cao assisting Han;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le sent his chief clerk on the left, Wang Xiu, to report his victories to the Han court. Liu Yao dispatched Guo Si, acting Minister of Works, to invest Le as Grand Preceptor and Commander-in-Chief, raise him to King of Zhao with extraordinary honors, and grant him the imperial escort on coming and going—the same privileges Cao Cao had enjoyed as regent of Han.

sentences.zh: 拜王修及其副劉茂皆為將軍，封列侯。

translations.literal: Wang Xiu and his deputy Liu Mao were both appointed generals and enfeoffed as ranked marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiu and his deputy Liu Mao were both made generals and enfeoffed as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 修舍人曹平樂從修至粟邑，因留仕漢，言於曜曰：「大司馬遣修等來，外表至誠，內覘大駕強弱，俟其覆命，將襲乘輿。」

translations.literal: Xiu's house attendant Cao Pingle followed Xiu to Suyi, then remained to serve Han and said to Yao: 'The Grand Marshal sent Xiu and the others outwardly with utmost sincerity but inwardly to observe the strength or weakness of Your Majesty's forces; when they return with their report, they will strike at the imperial carriage.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's retainer Cao Pingle had accompanied him as far as Suyi, then stayed behind to serve the Han court. He told Yao, 'The Grand Marshal sent Xiu and his party with a show of utmost loyalty, but their real aim was to gauge Your Majesty's strength. Once they bring back their report, they mean to strike at the imperial train.'

sentences.zh: 時漢兵實疲弊，曜信之。

translations.literal: At that time Han troops were in truth worn and exhausted, and Yao believed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Han armies were in truth exhausted, and Yao believed him.

sentences.zh: 乃追汜還，斬修於市。

translations.literal: He then recalled Guo Si and executed Xiu in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Guo Si and had Xiu beheaded in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 三月，勒還至襄國。

translations.literal: Third month: Le returned to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Le returned to Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 劉茂逃歸，言修死狀。

translations.literal: Liu Mao fled back and reported how Xiu had died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mao escaped and brought word of Xiu's execution.

sentences.zh: 勒大怒曰：「孤事劉氏，於人臣之職有加矣。

translations.literal: Le said in great anger: 'I have served the Liu house beyond what is owed by a subject's duty.
translations.idiomatic: Le flew into a rage. 'I have served the Liu house far beyond what any subject owes,' he said.

sentences.zh: 彼之基業，皆孤所為，今既得志，還欲相圖。

translations.literal: Their foundation was all my doing; now that they have achieved their aims, they still wish to plot against me.
translations.idiomatic: Their whole foundation was my work. Now that they have what they wanted, they turn around and plot against me.

sentences.zh: 趙王、趙帝，孤自為之，何待於彼邪！」

translations.literal: King of Zhao, Emperor of Zhao—I shall make these titles myself; why wait on them!'
translations.idiomatic: King of Zhao, Emperor of Zhao—I will take those titles myself. Why should I wait on them?'

sentences.zh: 乃誅曹平樂三族。

translations.literal: He then executed the three clans of Cao Pingle.
translations.idiomatic: He then exterminated Cao Pingle's clan to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 帝令群臣議郊祀，尚書令刁協等以為宜須還洛乃修之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the ministers to discuss suburban sacrifices; Minister of Works Diao Xie and others held that they should wait until the return to Luoyang before undertaking them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his ministers to debate the suburban sacrifices. Diao Xie, Director of the Masters of Writing, and others argued that the rites should wait until the court returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 司徒荀組等曰：「漢獻帝都許，即行郊祀。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Xun Zu and others said: 'When Emperor Xian of Han made his capital at Xu, he at once performed the suburban sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Xun Zu and others replied, 'When Emperor Xian of Han made Xu his capital, he performed the suburban sacrifices right away.

sentences.zh: 何必洛邑！」

translations.literal: Why must it be Luoyang!'
translations.idiomatic: Why insist on Luoyang?'

sentences.zh: 帝從之，立郊丘於建康城之巳地。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this view and established the suburban mound in the si quarter of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and established the suburban altar in the si quarter of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，帝親祀南郊。

translations.literal: On xinmao the Emperor personally sacrificed at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinmao the emperor personally offered sacrifice at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 以未有北郊，並地祗合祭之，詔：「琅邪恭王宜稱皇考。」

translations.literal: Because there was not yet a northern suburb, the earth spirit was worshipped together with Heaven; an edict said: 'The Respectful Prince of Langye should be styled Imperial Father.'
translations.idiomatic: With no northern suburban altar yet in place, he combined the rites for the earth spirit with those for Heaven. An edict declared that the Respectful Prince of Langye should be styled Imperial Father.

sentences.zh: 賀循曰：「《禮》，子不敢以己爵加於父。」

translations.literal: He Xun said: 'According to the Rites, a son does not dare place his own rank above his father's.'
translations.idiomatic: He Xun objected: 'The Rites teach that a son must not set his own rank above his father's.'

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The plan was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 初，蓬陂塢主陳川自稱陳留太守。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chen Chuan, master of the Pengpo stockade, styled himself Administrator of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chen Chuan, lord of the Pengpo stockade, had proclaimed himself Administrator of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 祖逖之攻樊雅也，川遣其將李頭助之。

translations.literal: When Zu Ti attacked Fan Ya, Chuan sent his general Li Tou to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Ti attacked Fan Ya, Chuan sent his general Li Tou to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 頭力戰有功，逖厚遇之。

translations.literal: Tou fought fiercely with merit, and Ti treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Tou fought with conspicuous valor, and Ti treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 頭每歎曰：「得此人為主，吾死無恨！」

translations.literal: Tou would often sigh and say: 'To have such a man as master— I could die without regret!'
translations.idiomatic: Tou often sighed, 'If only a man like this were my lord, I could die without regret!'

sentences.zh: 川聞而殺之。

translations.literal: When Chuan heard of this he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuan heard of this, he had him killed.

sentences.zh: 頭黨馮寵帥其眾降逖，川益怒，大掠豫州諸郡，逖遣兵擊破之。

translations.literal: Tou's follower Feng Chong led the troops in surrender to Ti; Chuan grew angrier, plundered widely through the commanderies of Yuzhou, and Ti sent troops who defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Tou's comrade Feng Chong led his men over to Zu Ti. Chuan, enraged, launched wide raids across Yuzhou until Ti sent forces and routed him.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，川以浚儀叛，降石勒。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Chuan rebelled with Junyi and submitted to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Chuan rebelled from Junyi and went over to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 周撫之敗走也，徐龕部將於藥追斬之，及朝廷論功，而劉遐先之；

translations.literal: When Zhou Fu was defeated and fled, Xu Kan's officer Yu Yao pursued and beheaded him; when the court discussed merit, Liu Xia reported first;
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou Fu's defeat and flight, Xu Kan's officer Yu Yao ran him down and killed him. When the court weighed rewards for the victory, Liu Xia claimed priority;

sentences.zh: 龕怒，以泰山叛，降石勒，自稱兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Kan was enraged, rebelled with Mount Tai, submitted to Shi Le, and styled himself Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kan, furious, rebelled from Taishan, submitted to Shi Le, and proclaimed himself Inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 漢主曜還，都長安，立妃羊氏為皇后，子熙為皇太子，封子襲為長樂王，闡為太原王，沖為淮南王，敞為齊王，高為魯王，徽為楚王；

translations.literal: The Han ruler Liu Yao returned and made his capital at Chang'an, installed his consort the Lady Yang as empress and his son Xi as crown prince, enfeoffed his sons Xi as Prince of Changle, Chan as Prince of Taiyuan, Chong as Prince of Huainan, Chang as Prince of Qi, Gao as Prince of Lu, and Hui as Prince of Chu;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao of Han returned to Chang'an as his capital. He made his consort Lady Yang empress and his son Xi crown prince, and enfeoffed his sons: Xi as Prince of Changle, Chan as Prince of Taiyuan, Chong as Prince of Huainan, Chang as Prince of Qi, Gao as Prince of Lu, and Hui as Prince of Chu;

sentences.zh: 諸宗室皆進封郡王。

translations.literal: all members of the imperial clan were advanced to princes of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: and advanced every member of the imperial clan to princely rank within their commanderies.

sentences.zh: 羊氏，即故惠帝后也。

translations.literal: The Lady Yang was none other than the former empress of Emperor Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang was none other than the former empress of Emperor Hui of Jin.

sentences.zh: 曜嘗問之曰：「吾何如司馬家兒？」

translations.literal: Yao once asked her: 'How do I compare with that boy of the Sima house?'
translations.idiomatic: Yao once asked her, 'How do I measure against that Sima boy?'

sentences.zh: 羊氏曰：「陛下開基之聖主，彼亡國之暗夫，何可並言！

translations.literal: The Lady Yang said: 'Your Majesty is a sage founding a new realm; he was a benighted man of a fallen state—how can they be spoken of together!
translations.idiomatic: She replied, 'Your Majesty is a sage who is founding a new realm; he was a benighted ruler of a fallen dynasty—there is no comparing the two!

sentences.zh: 彼貴為帝王，有一婦、一子及身三耳，曾不能庇。

translations.literal: Though he was exalted as Son of Heaven, he had only one wife, one son, and his own person—three in all—and could not even protect them.
translations.idiomatic: Though he sat as Son of Heaven, he had only a wife, a son, and his own person—three lives in all—and could not even protect them.

sentences.zh: 妾於爾時，實不欲生，意謂世間男子皆然。

translations.literal: At that time I truly did not wish to live, and supposed that all men in the world were like that.
translations.idiomatic: In those days I truly wished I were dead; I thought every man in the world must be the same.

sentences.zh: 自奉巾櫛已來，始知天下自有丈夫耳！」

translations.literal: Since I have served at your comb and towel, I have come to know that the world truly has real men!'
translations.idiomatic: Only since I entered your service have I learned that the world still holds a true man!'

sentences.zh: 曜甚寵之，頗干預國事。

translations.literal: Yao favored her greatly, and she intervened considerably in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yao doted on her, and she came to meddle extensively in affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 南陽王保自稱晉王，改元建康，置百官，以張寔為征西大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Prince Bao of Nanyang styled himself King of Jin, changed the era name to Jiankang, established the full bureaucracy, and appointed Zhang Shi Grand General Who Conquers the West with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Bao of Nanyang proclaimed himself King of Jin, adopted the era name Jiankang, set up a full court, and appointed Zhang Shi Grand General Who Conquers the West with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 陳安自稱秦州刺史，降於漢，又降於成。

translations.literal: Chen An styled himself Inspector of Qinzhou, submitted to Han, then submitted to Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An proclaimed himself Inspector of Qinzhou, submitted to Han, then switched to Cheng Han.

sentences.zh: 上邽大饑，士眾困迫，張春奉保之南安祁山。

translations.literal: Shanggui suffered great famine; soldiers and people were in distress, and Zhang Chun escorted Bao to Qishan in Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck Shanggui; troops and civilians were desperate, and Zhang Chun led Bao to Qishan in Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 寔遣韓璞帥步騎五千救之；

translations.literal: Shi sent Han Pu at the head of five thousand foot and horse to rescue him;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi sent Han Pu with five thousand infantry and cavalry to relieve him;

sentences.zh: 陳安退保綿諸，保歸上邽。

translations.literal: Chen An withdrew to defend Mianzhu, and Bao returned to Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An fell back to Mianzhu, and Bao returned to Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 未幾，保復為安所逼，寔遣其將宋毅救之，安乃退。

translations.literal: Before long Bao was again pressed by An; Shi sent his general Song Yi to rescue him, and An then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Bao was harried again by Chen An; Zhang Shi sent his general Song Yi to the rescue, and An withdrew.

sentences.zh: 江東大饑，詔百官各上封事。

translations.literal: The region east of the Yangzi suffered great famine; an edict ordered all officials to submit sealed memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Famine ravaged the lands east of the Yangzi, and the emperor ordered every official to submit sealed memorials with policy recommendations.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史應詹上疏曰：「元康以來，賤《經》尚道，以玄虛宏放為夷達，以儒術清儉為鄙俗。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yizhou Ying Zhan submitted a memorial saying: 'Since the Yuankang era the Classics have been despised and the Way exalted; vagueness and broad unconventionality were taken for transcendent attainment, while Confucian learning and plain frugality were deemed vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhan, Inspector of Yizhou, wrote: 'Since the Yuankang era the Classics have been scorned while empty speculation has been prized; vagueness and libertine display pass for sophistication, while Confucian learning and plain frugality are dismissed as vulgar.

sentences.zh: 宜崇獎儒官，以新俗化。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to honor and encourage Confucian officials in order to renew custom and transform the people.'
translations.idiomatic: The court should honor Confucian scholars and officials so as to renew the manners of the age.'

sentences.zh: 祖逖攻陳川於蓬關，石勒遣石虎將兵五萬救之，戰於浚儀，逖兵敗，退屯梁國。

translations.literal: Zu Ti attacked Chen Chuan at Peng Pass; Shi Le sent Shi Hu with fifty thousand troops to rescue him; they fought at Junyi, Ti's army was defeated, and he withdrew to garrison at Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti attacked Chen Chuan at Peng Pass. Shi Le sent Shi Hu with fifty thousand men to relieve him. They fought at Junyi; Zu Ti was beaten and fell back to Liang.

sentences.zh: 勒又遣桃豹將兵至蓬關，逖退屯淮南。

translations.literal: Le also sent Tao Bao with troops to Peng Pass, and Ti withdrew to garrison at Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Le then sent Tao Bao to Peng Pass, and Zu Ti withdrew to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 虎徙川部眾五千戶於襄國，留豹守川故城。

translations.literal: Hu moved five thousand households of Chuan's followers to Xiangguo and left Bao to hold Chuan's former city.
translations.idiomatic: Hu relocated five thousand of Chuan's households to Xiangguo and left Bao to hold Chuan's old stronghold.

sentences.zh: 石勒遣石虎擊鮮卑日六延於朔方，大破之，斬首二萬級，俘虜三萬餘人。

translations.literal: Shi Le sent Shi Hu to attack the Xianbei chief Riliuyan at Shuofang, routed him utterly, took twenty thousand heads, and captured more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le sent Shi Hu against the Xianbei leader Riliuyan at Shuofang, crushed his forces, took twenty thousand heads, and captured more than thirty thousand people.

sentences.zh: 孔萇攻幽州諸郡，悉取之。

translations.literal: Kong Chang attacked the commanderies of Youzhou and took them all.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chang overran the commanderies of Youzhou and seized them all.

sentences.zh: 段匹磾士眾饑散，欲移保上谷，代王鬱律勒兵將擊之，匹磾棄妻子奔樂陵，依邵續。

translations.literal: Duan Pidi's soldiers and people, starving, scattered; wishing to move and hold Shanggu, the Prince of Dai Yulü led troops to strike him; Pidi abandoned wife and children and fled to Leling to rely on Shao Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi's troops, starving, broke apart. As he tried to withdraw to Shanggu, the Prince of Dai Yulü marched against him. Pidi abandoned his wife and children and fled to Leling, where he placed himself under Shao Xu's protection.

sentences.zh: 曹嶷遣使賂石勒，請以河為境，勒許之。

translations.literal: Cao Ni sent envoys with gifts to bribe Shi Le, asking to take the Yellow River as the border; Le agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ni sent envoys bearing gifts to Shi Le, proposing the Yellow River as their mutual border, and Le agreed.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史周訪擊杜曾，大破之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Liangzhou Zhou Fang attacked Du Zeng and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang, Inspector of Liangzhou, attacked Du Zeng and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 馬俊等執曾以降，訪斬之，並獲荊州刺史第五猗，送於武昌。

translations.literal: Ma Jun and others seized Zeng and brought him in submission; Fang beheaded him and also captured Inspector of Jingzhou Di Yi, sending him to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jun and others seized Zeng and surrendered him. Fang executed him, also captured Di Yi, Inspector of Jingzhou, and sent him to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 訪以猗本中朝所署，加有時望，白王敦不宜殺，敦不聽而斬之。

translations.literal: Fang, because Yi had originally been appointed by the central court and moreover enjoyed repute in his time, reported to Wang Dun that he should not be killed; Dun did not listen and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang urged Wang Dun not to kill Yi, noting that he had been appointed by the central court and still commanded respect; Dun ignored him and had Yi executed.

sentences.zh: 初，敦患杜曾難制，謂訪曰：「若擒曾，當相論為荊州。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Dun had worried that Du Zeng was hard to control and said to Fang: 'If you capture Zeng, I shall consider making you Inspector of Jingzhou.'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Dun had complained that Du Zeng was hard to subdue and told Fang, 'If you take Zeng, I will see that you receive Jingzhou.'

sentences.zh: 及曾死而敦不用。

translations.literal: When Zeng was dead Dun did not follow through.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng was dead, Dun went back on his word.

sentences.zh: 王廙在荊州，多殺陶侃將佐；

translations.literal: Wang Yi was in Jingzhou and killed many of Tao Kan's officers and aides;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi, as governor of Jingzhou, executed many of Tao Kan's officers and aides;

sentences.zh: 以皇甫方回為侃所敬，責其不詣己，收斬之。

translations.literal: because Huangfu Fanghui was respected by Kan, he blamed him for not coming to call on himself, seized him, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: and because Huangfu Fanghui was a man Tao Kan revered, Yi blamed him for failing to pay a courtesy call, seized him, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 士民怨怒，上下不安。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners were resentful and angry; high and low were unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners seethed with resentment, and the province was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，征廙為散騎常侍，以周訪代為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of this he recalled Yi as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and replaced him with Zhou Fang as Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the emperor, he recalled Yi to court as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and appointed Zhou Fang Inspector of Jingzhou in his place.

sentences.zh: 王敦忌訪威名，意難之。

translations.literal: Wang Dun resented Fang's renown and was reluctant in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun, jealous of Fang's reputation, bridled at the appointment.

sentences.zh: 從事中郎郭舒說敦曰：「鄙州雖荒弊，乃用武之國，不可以假人，宜自領之，訪為梁州足矣。」

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman Guo Shu urged Dun: 'Though this province is remote and impoverished, it is a land that employs force of arms and cannot be lent to another; you should hold it yourself—Fang as Inspector of Liangzhou is enough.'
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shu, his attendant gentleman, urged him: 'Jingzhou may be poor and remote, but it is a martial province and must not be handed to another. You should keep it yourself; making Fang Inspector of Liangzhou is honor enough.'

sentences.zh: 敦從之。

translations.literal: Dun followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Dun took his advice.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙子，詔加訪安南將軍，餘如故。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on bingzi an edict added to Fang the title General Who Pacifies the South, the rest remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day bingzi, an edict promoted Fang to General Who Pacifies the South while leaving his other titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 訪大怒，敦手書譬解，並遺玉環、玉碗以申厚意。

translations.literal: Fang was greatly angered; Dun wrote a personal letter of explanation and also sent jade rings and a jade bowl to express deep regard.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was furious. Dun wrote him a personal letter of apology and sent jade rings and a jade bowl as tokens of esteem.

sentences.zh: 訪抵之於地，曰：「吾豈賈豎，可以寶悅邪！」

translations.literal: Fang dashed them to the ground and said: 'Am I some merchant who can be pleased with treasure!'
translations.idiomatic: Fang hurled them to the ground. 'Do you take me for a peddler,' he cried, 'to be bought off with jewels?'

sentences.zh: 訪在襄陽，務農訓兵，陰有圖敦之志，守宰有缺輒補，然後言上；

translations.literal: Fang at Xiangyang devoted himself to farming and training troops, secretly harboring the intent to move against Dun; whenever a local post was vacant he filled it first and only then reported upward;
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang, Fang devoted himself to agriculture and drill, secretly planning against Dun. Whenever a local post fell vacant he filled it on his own authority and only then informed the court;

sentences.zh: 敦患之，而不能制。

translations.literal: Dun was troubled by this but could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: Dun chafed at this but could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 魏該為胡寇所逼，自宜陽帥眾南遷新野，助周訪討杜曾有功，拜順陽太守。

translations.literal: Wei Gai, pressed by barbarian raiders, led his followers south from Yiyang to settle at Xinye; in assisting Zhou Fang against Du Zeng he rendered merit and was appointed Administrator of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by barbarian raiders, Wei Gai led his people south from Yiyang to Xinye. He aided Zhou Fang against Du Zeng and was rewarded with the post of Administrator of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 趙固死，郭誦留屯陽翟，石生屢攻之，不能克。

translations.literal: Zhao Gu died; Guo Song remained garrisoned at Yangzhai; Shi Sheng attacked repeatedly but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao Gu's death, Guo Song held Yangzhai. Shi Sheng attacked again and again but could not take the city.

sentences.zh: 漢主曜立宗廟、社稷、南北郊於長安，詔曰：「吾之先，興於北方。

translations.literal: The Han ruler Liu Yao established ancestral temples, the altars of soil and grain, and the southern and northern suburban altars at Chang'an, and issued an edict: 'My ancestors rose in the north.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao of Han established ancestral temples, the altars of soil and grain, and the suburban altars at Chang'an. His edict read: 'Our forebears rose in the north.

sentences.zh: 光文立漢宗廟以從民望。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwen established Han ancestral temples to follow the people's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwen set up Han ancestral temples to satisfy popular expectation.

sentences.zh: 今宜改國號，以單于為祖。

translations.literal: Now the dynastic name should be changed, with the Chanyu as ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Now the dynastic name should be changed, with the Chanyu as our founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 亟議以聞！」

translations.literal: Debate this quickly and report!'
translations.idiomatic: Deliberate at once and report your conclusions!'

sentences.zh: 群臣奏：「光文始封盧奴伯，陛下又王中山；

translations.literal: The ministers memorialized: 'Emperor Guangwen was first enfeoffed as Marquis of Lunu; Your Majesty was also made Prince of Zhongshan;
translations.idiomatic: The ministers replied: 'Emperor Guangwen was first enfeoffed as Marquis of Lunu, and Your Majesty was made Prince of Zhongshan;

sentences.zh: 中山，趙分也，請改國號為趙。」

translations.literal: Zhongshan is the allotment of Zhao— we ask that the dynastic name be changed to Zhao.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan is the Zhao allotment. We ask that the dynastic name be changed to Zhao.'

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 以冒頓配天，光文配上帝。

translations.literal: Modu was paired with Heaven; Guangwen was paired with the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Modu was worshipped as counterpart to Heaven; Guangwen as counterpart to the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 徐龕寇掠濟、岱，破東莞。

translations.literal: Xu Kan raided Ji and Dai, breaking through Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Kan raided Ji and Dai and overran Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 帝問將帥可以討龕者於王導，導以為太子左衛率太山羊鑒，龕之州裡冠族，必能制之。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Wang Dao which commander could campaign against Kan; Dao thought the Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, Yang Jian of Taishan—a leading clan of Kan's own province—would surely be able to control him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Wang Dao which general could subdue Kan. Dao named Yang Jian of Taishan, Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard—a leading man of Kan's own province who would surely bring him to heel.

sentences.zh: 鑒深辭，才非將帥，郗鑒亦表鑒非才，不可使；

translations.literal: Jian declined deeply, saying his talent was not that of a commander; Xi Jian also memorialized that Jian lacked the ability and should not be sent;
translations.idiomatic: Jian declined firmly, protesting that he lacked a commander's gifts; Xi Jian also memorialized that Jian was unfit for the post;

sentences.zh: 導不從。

translations.literal: Dao did not follow them.
translations.idiomatic: Dao would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，以羊鑒為征虜將軍、征討都督，督徐州刺史蔡豹、臨淮太守劉遐、鮮卑段文鴦等討之。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month: Yang Jian was made General Who Captures Barbarians and Commander of the Campaign, directing Inspector of Xuzhou Cai Bao, Administrator of Linhuai Liu Xia, the Xianbei Duan Wenyang, and others against him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, Yang Jian was appointed General Who Captures Barbarians and supreme commander of the campaign, directing Cai Bao, Inspector of Xuzhou, Liu Xia, Administrator of Linhuai, the Xianbei chief Duan Wenyang, and others against Kan.

sentences.zh: 冬，石勒左、右長史張敬、張賓、左、右司馬張屈六、程遐等，勸勒稱尊號，勒不許。

translations.literal: Winter: Shi Le's Left and Right Chief Clerks Zhang Jing and Zhang Bin, Left and Right Majors Zhang Qu and Cheng Xia, and others urged Le to assume an exalted title; Le did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, Zhang Jing and Zhang Bin, Le's chief clerks on left and right, together with Zhang Qu and Cheng Xia, his majors on left and right, urged him to take an imperial title. Le refused.

sentences.zh: 十一月，將佐等復請勒稱大將軍、大單于、領冀州牧、趙王，依漢昭烈在蜀、魏武在鄴故事，以河內等二十四郡為趙國，太守皆為內史，准《禹貢》，復冀州之境，以大單于鎮撫百蠻，罷並、朔、司三州，通置部司以監之；

translations.literal: Eleventh month: generals and aides again asked Le to style himself Grand General, Grand Chanyu, Governor of Jizhou, and King of Zhao, following the precedents of Han's Founder in Shu and Wei Wu at Ye; the twenty-four commanderies including Henei were made the State of Zhao, administrators all became interior ministers, according with the Tribute of Yu the borders of Jizhou were restored, the Grand Chanyu was to pacify the hundred barbarians, the three provinces Bing, Shuo, and Si were abolished and overseers of departments were set up throughout to supervise them;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month his generals and staff renewed their plea that he take the titles Grand General, Grand Chanyu, Governor of Jizhou, and King of Zhao—following the precedents of Liu Bei in Shu and Cao Cao at Ye. Twenty-four commanderies including Henei would form the State of Zhao, with every administrator made an interior minister; borders would be redrawn to match the Tribute of Yu's description of Jizhou; the Grand Chanyu would pacify the barbarian peoples; and the three provinces Bing, Shuo, and Si would be abolished in favor of supervisory offices;

sentences.zh: 勒許之。

translations.literal: Le agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Le consented.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，即趙王位，大赦，依春秋時列國稱元年。

translations.literal: On wuyin he assumed the kingship of Zhao, proclaimed a general amnesty, and following the practice of the feudal states in the Spring and Autumn era styled this year one.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuyin he assumed the title King of Zhao, proclaimed a general amnesty, and—following the custom of the Spring and Autumn states—dated his reign from year one.

sentences.zh: 初，勒以世亂，律令煩多，命法曹令史貫志，採集其要，作《辛亥制》五千文；

translations.literal: Earlier, because the age was chaotic and statutes numerous, Le ordered the law-office clerk Guan Zhi to gather the essentials and compose the Xinhaizhi Regulations in five thousand characters;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, finding the age chaotic and the laws unwieldy, Le had Guan Zhi of the law office distill their essentials into the Xinhaizhi Regulations, five thousand characters in all;

sentences.zh: 施行十餘年，乃用律令。

translations.literal: They were implemented for more than ten years before the full statutes and ordinances were employed.
translations.idiomatic: These regulations governed the realm for more than a decade before the full body of statutes came into force.

sentences.zh: 以理曹參軍上黨續鹹為律學祭酒；

translations.literal: Xu Xian of Shangdang, an aide in the Bureau of Justice, was made Libationer of Legal Studies;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xian of Shangdang, an aide in the Bureau of Justice, was appointed Libationer of Legal Studies;

sentences.zh: 鹹用法詳平，國人稱之。

translations.literal: Xian applied the law with detail and fairness, and the people of the state praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian applied the law with meticulous fairness, and the people praised him.

sentences.zh: 以中壘將軍支雄、游擊將軍王陽領門臣祭酒，專主胡人辭訟，重禁胡人，不得陵侮衣冠華族，號胡為國人。

translations.literal: General of the Central Ramparts Zhi Xiong and General Who Sweeps Away Bandits Wang Yang were made Libationers of the Court Retainers, exclusively handling lawsuits among the barbarians; barbarians were strictly forbidden to insult or bully the gentry in caps and robes, and barbarians were styled 'people of the state.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Xiong, General of the Central Ramparts, and Wang Yang, General Who Sweeps Away Bandits, were put in charge of barbarian litigation as Libationers of the Court Retainers. Barbarians were strictly forbidden to bully the Chinese gentry, and were officially styled 'people of the state.'

sentences.zh: 遣使循行州郡，勸課農桑。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to tour the provinces and commanderies and encourage farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched envoys to tour the provinces and commanderies, urging the people to farm and raise silkworms.

sentences.zh: 朝會始用天子禮樂、衣冠、儀物，從容可觀矣。

translations.literal: At court assemblies the ritual music, caps and robes, and ceremonial objects of the Son of Heaven were first used, and proceedings became dignified and impressive.
translations.idiomatic: Court assemblies now employed the ritual music, robes, and ceremonial regalia of the Son of Heaven, and the proceedings took on a dignified, imposing air.

sentences.zh: 加張賓大執法，專總朝政；

translations.literal: Zhang Bin was advanced to Grand Enforcer and given exclusive charge of court government;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin was promoted to Grand Enforcer with exclusive control of the government;

sentences.zh: 以石虎為單于元輔、都督禁衛諸軍事，尋加驃騎將軍、侍中、開府，賜爵中山公；

translations.literal: Shi Hu was made Chanyu Chief Minister and Director of All Palace Guard Military Affairs, soon after added as General of Agile Cavalry, Palace Attendant, and with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhongshan;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu was made Chanyu Chief Minister and commander of all palace-guard forces, then promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, Palace Attendant, and Director with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhongshan;

sentences.zh: 自餘群臣，授位進爵各有差。

translations.literal: the remaining ministers received offices and advances in rank each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: the remaining ministers received offices and promotions according to their merits.

sentences.zh: 張賓任遇優顯，群臣莫及；

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's appointment and favor were outstandingly prominent, and no minister could match him;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin stood above every other minister in rank and favor;

sentences.zh: 而廉虛敬慎，開懷下士，屏絕阿私，以身帥物，入則盡規，出則歸美。

translations.literal: yet he was modest, reverent, and cautious, open-hearted toward scholars, shut out flattery and favoritism, led others by his own example, offered full counsel in private, and in public attributed merit to others.
translations.idiomatic: yet he remained modest, reverent, and open-handed with scholars, shunning flattery and private favor. He led by example, gave his lord frank counsel in private, and in public gave credit to others.

sentences.zh: 勒甚重之，每朝，常為之正容貌，簡辭令，呼曰右侯而不敢名。

translations.literal: Le valued him greatly; at every court session he would compose his bearing and choose his words for Bin's sake, addressing him as 'Lord on the Right' and not daring to use his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Le held him in the highest regard. At every court session he composed his bearing and chose his words carefully, addressing him as 'Lord on the Right' rather than daring to speak his name.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙亥，大赦。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on yihai: a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day yihai, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 平州刺史崔毖，自以中州人望，鎮遼東，而士民多歸慕容廆，心不平。

translations.literal: Inspector of Pingzhou Cui Bi, considering himself a man of Central Plains standing garrisoning Liaodong, was inwardly displeased that gentry and commoners mostly went over to Murong Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Bi, Inspector of Pingzhou, had been posted to Liaodong as a man of Central Plains standing, but found that most of the local gentry and commoners had rallied to Murong Hui, and he resented it.

sentences.zh: 數遣使招之，皆不至，意廆拘留之，乃陰說高句麗、段氏、宇文氏，使共攻之，約滅廆，分其地。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent envoys to summon them, but none came; thinking Hui was detaining them, he secretly urged Koguryo, the Duan clan, and the Yuwen clan to attack together, agreeing that when Hui was destroyed they would divide his territory.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys again and again to summon them, but none came. Convinced that Hui was holding them back, he secretly persuaded Koguryo, the Duan clan, and the Yuwen clan to join in an attack, promising to divide Hui's territory once he was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 毖所親勃海高瞻力諫，毖不從。

translations.literal: Gao Zhan of Bohai, whom Bi favored, remonstrated forcefully, but Bi did not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhan of Bohai, a man Bi trusted, argued strenuously against the plan, but Bi would not listen.

sentences.zh: 三國合兵伐廆。

translations.literal: The three states united their armies to attack Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The three powers combined their forces to attack Murong Hui.

sentences.zh: 諸將請擊之，廆曰：「彼為崔毖所誘，欲邀一切之利。

translations.literal: The generals asked to strike them; Hui said: 'They have been enticed by Cui Bi and wish to seize every advantage at once.
translations.idiomatic: His generals urged an immediate attack. Hui said, 'Cui Bi has lured them here, and they mean to seize every advantage at once.

sentences.zh: 軍勢初合，其鋒甚銳，不可與戰，當固守以挫之。

translations.literal: Their forces have just combined and their edge is very sharp—we cannot fight them; we should hold fast to wear them down.
translations.idiomatic: Their armies have only just joined, and their momentum is at its peak. We must not meet them in battle; we should hold our walls and wear them down.

sentences.zh: 彼烏合而來，既無統壹，莫相歸服，久必攜貳，一則疑吾與毖詐而覆之，二則三國自相猜忌。

translations.literal: They have come in a mob without unity, and none obeys another; before long they will surely split—first suspecting that I and Bi are plotting to turn on them together, second growing suspicious of one another among the three states.
translations.idiomatic: They are a mob without unity, and none will obey another. Before long they will fall apart—first suspecting that Bi and I are plotting to turn on them together, then turning suspicious of one another among the three allies.

sentences.zh: 待其人情離貳，然後擊之，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: When their hearts are divided and estranged, then strike them—they will surely be broken.'
translations.idiomatic: When their alliance has rotted from within, we will strike, and they will surely be broken.'

sentences.zh: 三國進攻棘城，廆閉門自守，遣使獨以牛酒犒宇文氏。

translations.literal: The three states advanced to attack Jicheng; Hui shut the gates and held the city, sending envoys with oxen and wine to feast only the Yuwen clan.
translations.idiomatic: The three allies advanced on Jicheng. Hui shut the gates and held the city, but sent envoys bearing oxen and wine to feast only the Yuwen clan.

sentences.zh: 二國疑宇文氏與廆有謀，各引兵歸。

translations.literal: The other two states suspected the Yuwen of plotting with Hui and each withdrew their troops.
translations.idiomatic: The other two allies suspected the Yuwen of colluding with Hui and withdrew their armies.

sentences.zh: 宇文大人悉獨官曰：「二國雖歸，吾當獨取之。」

translations.literal: The Yuwen chieftain Xiduguan said: 'Though the two states have withdrawn, I shall take it alone.'
translations.idiomatic: The Yuwen chieftain Xiduguan said, 'The other two may have gone home, but I will take Jicheng on my own.'

sentences.zh: 宇文氏士卒數十萬，連營四十里。

translations.literal: The Yuwen had several hundred thousand soldiers, their camps stretching for forty li.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuwen mustered several hundred thousand men, their camps stretching for forty li.

sentences.zh: 廆使召其子翰於徒河。

translations.literal: Hui sent to summon his son Han from Tuhe.
translations.idiomatic: Hui summoned his son Han from Tuhe.

sentences.zh: 翰遣使白廆曰：「悉獨官譽國為寇，彼眾我寡，易以計破，難以力勝。

translations.literal: Han sent a messenger to report to Hui: 'Xiduguan has made a name raiding states; they are many and we are few—easy to defeat by stratagem, hard to overcome by force.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent word to his father: 'Xiduguan has built his reputation raiding other states. They outnumber us; this is a fight to be won by stratagem, not brute force.

sentences.zh: 今城中之眾，足以禦寇，翰請為奇兵於外，伺其間而擊之，內外俱奮，使彼震駭不知所備，破之必矣。

translations.literal: The forces in the city now are enough to resist the enemy; Han asks to serve as a surprise force outside, watch for an opening and strike, with inner and outer both fighting hard so that they are shaken and do not know how to prepare—breaking them is certain.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison is strong enough to hold the city. Let me take a mobile force outside, watch for an opening, and strike. With attacks from within and without, they will be thrown into panic and confusion, and we will surely break them.

sentences.zh: 今並兵為一，彼得專意攻城，無復它虞，非策之得者也。

translations.literal: If we combine all forces into one, they can concentrate on storming the city with no other worries—that is not a winning plan.
translations.idiomatic: If we mass every man in the city, they can concentrate on the siege with no other worry. That is not sound strategy.

sentences.zh: 且示眾以怯，恐士氣不戰先沮矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover, to show the army our timidity may cause morale to collapse before battle.'
translations.idiomatic: And if we show fear before our own men, their spirit may collapse before a blow is struck.'

sentences.zh: 廆猶疑之。

translations.literal: Hui still hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: Hui still hesitated.

sentences.zh: 遼東韓壽言於廆曰：「悉獨官有憑陵之志，將驕卒惰，軍不堅密，若奇兵卒起，掎其無備，必破之策也。」

translations.literal: Han Shou of Liaodong said to Hui: 'Xiduguan has the will to bully others; his generals are arrogant and his soldiers lax, the army not tightly disciplined—if a surprise force rises suddenly and strikes where they are unprepared, that is the plan that will surely break them.'
translations.idiomatic: Han Shou of Liaodong urged Hui, 'Xiduguan is overbearing, his officers arrogant and his troops slack. Their formation is loose. A sudden strike where they are unprepared is the sure way to break them.'

sentences.zh: 廆乃聽翰留徒河。

translations.literal: Hui then allowed Han to remain at Tuhe.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then let Han stay at Tuhe.

sentences.zh: 悉獨官聞之，曰：「翰素名驍果，今不入城，或能為患，當先取之，城不足憂。」

translations.literal: When Xiduguan heard of this he said: 'Han has long been famed for fierceness and resolve; now that he does not enter the city, he may become a danger—we should take him first; the city is not worth worrying over.'
translations.idiomatic: When Xiduguan heard of this, he said, 'Han has long been famed for courage and dash. If he stays outside the walls, he may become a threat. We should deal with him first; the city itself is no great worry.'

sentences.zh: 乃分遣數千騎襲翰。

translations.literal: He then detached several thousand horsemen to raid Han.
translations.idiomatic: He detached several thousand horsemen to strike at Han.

sentences.zh: 翰知之，詐為段氏使者，逆於道曰：「慕容翰久為吾患，聞當擊之，吾已嚴兵相待，宜速進也！」

translations.literal: Han learned of this, posed as an envoy of the Duan clan, and met them on the road saying: 'Murong Han has long been our trouble; hearing you are to attack him, I have already drawn up troops to await you—advance quickly!'
translations.idiomatic: Han learned of the move, disguised his men as Duan envoys, and met the Yuwen on the road. 'Murong Han has long been our scourge,' he said. 'We heard you were coming to attack him and have drawn up our troops to join you. Press on quickly!'

sentences.zh: 使者既去，翰即出城，設伏以待之。

translations.literal: After the envoys had gone, Han went out of the city and set an ambush to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Once the envoys had gone, Han marched out and laid an ambush.

sentences.zh: 宇文氏之騎見使者，大喜馳行，不復設備，進入伏中。

translations.literal: The Yuwen horsemen, seeing the envoys, were greatly pleased and galloped on without setting guards again, and entered the ambush.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuwen cavalry, delighted by the message, galloped ahead without taking precautions and rode straight into the trap.

sentences.zh: 翰奮擊，盡獲之，乘勝徑進，遣間使語廆出兵大戰。

translations.literal: Han struck fiercely and captured them all, then pressed the victory straight forward and sent a secret messenger to tell Hui to bring out the army for a great battle.
translations.idiomatic: Han struck with all his force and captured them to the last man, then pressed the victory and sent a secret messenger urging Hui to march out for the decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 廆使其子皝與長史裴嶷將精銳為前鋒，自將大兵繼之。

translations.literal: Hui sent his son Huang and Chief Clerk Pei Yi at the head of picked troops as the vanguard, and himself led the main army after them.
translations.idiomatic: Hui sent his son Huang and Chief Clerk Pei Yi ahead with picked troops as the vanguard, and followed with the main army.

sentences.zh: 悉獨官初不設備，聞廆至，驚，悉眾出戰。

translations.literal: Xiduguan had made no preparations at first; hearing Hui had come, he was alarmed and led out his entire force to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Xiduguan, caught unprepared, was alarmed when he heard Hui was coming and led out his entire army to fight.

sentences.zh: 前鋒始交，翰將千騎從旁直入其營，縱火焚之。

translations.literal: As the vanguards had just joined battle, Han led a thousand horsemen straight into their camp from the side and set fires to burn it.
translations.idiomatic: As the vanguards clashed, Han led a thousand horsemen in a flanking charge straight into the Yuwen camp and set it ablaze.

sentences.zh: 眾皆惶擾，不知所為。

translations.literal: The masses were all alarmed and confused, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: The army panicked, not knowing which way to turn.

sentences.zh: 遂大敗，悉獨官僅為身免。

translations.literal: They were utterly defeated, and Xiduguan barely escaped with his own person.
translations.idiomatic: They were routed utterly, and Xiduguan barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 廆盡俘其眾，獲皇帝玉璽三紐。

translations.literal: Hui captured all their followers and obtained three imperial jade seals with cords.
translations.idiomatic: Hui took the entire Yuwen force prisoner and seized three imperial jade seals.

sentences.zh: 崔毖聞之，懼，使其兄子燾詣棘城偽賀。

translations.literal: When Cui Bi heard of this he was afraid and sent his elder brother's son Tao to Jicheng with a false congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Bi heard the news he was terrified and sent his nephew Tao to Jicheng with hollow congratulations.

sentences.zh: 會三國使者亦至，請和，曰：「非我本意，崔平州教我耳。」

translations.literal: It happened that envoys from the three states also arrived seeking peace, saying: 'This was not our original intent—Inspector Cui of Pingzhou urged us on.'
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from the three allies also arrived seeking peace. 'This was not our own wish,' they said. 'Inspector Cui of Pingzhou incited us.'

sentences.zh: 廆以示燾，臨之以兵，燾懼，首服。

translations.literal: Hui showed this to Tao and confronted him with troops; Tao was afraid and confessed in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Hui confronted Tao with this evidence and an armed display. Tao, terrified, confessed everything.

sentences.zh: 廆乃遣燾歸謂毖曰：「降者上策，走者下策也。」

translations.literal: Hui then sent Tao back to tell Bi: 'To submit is the upper plan; to flee is the lower plan.'
translations.idiomatic: Hui sent Tao back with a message for Bi: 'Surrender is the wise course; flight is the desperate one.'

sentences.zh: 引兵隨之。

translations.literal: He led troops after him.
translations.idiomatic: Then he marched in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 毖與數十騎棄家奔高句麗，其眾悉降於廆。

translations.literal: Bi fled with several dozen horsemen, abandoning his household to Koguryo, and all his followers submitted to Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Bi fled with a few dozen horsemen, abandoning his household for Koguryo, and all his followers submitted to Hui.

sentences.zh: 廆以其子仁為征虜將軍，鎮遼東，官府、市裡，案堵如故。

translations.literal: Hui made his son Ren General Who Captures Barbarians to garrison Liaodong; government offices and market wards remained as orderly as before.
translations.idiomatic: Hui appointed his son Ren General Who Captures Barbarians to govern Liaodong, and government offices and markets continued undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 高句麗將如奴子據於河城，廆遣將軍張統掩擊，擒之，俘其眾千餘家；

translations.literal: The Koguryo general Runuzi held Hecheng; Hui sent General Zhang Tong in a surprise attack, captured him, and took more than a thousand of his households captive;
translations.idiomatic: The Koguryo general Runuzi held Hecheng. Hui sent General Zhang Tong in a surprise attack, captured him, and took more than a thousand households prisoner;

sentences.zh: 以崔燾、高瞻、韓恆、石琮歸於棘城，待以客禮。

translations.literal: Cui Tao, Gao Zhan, Han Heng, and Shi Cong were brought back to Jicheng and treated with the courtesy due guests.
translations.idiomatic: and brought Cui Tao, Gao Zhan, Han Heng, and Shi Cong back to Jicheng, treating them as honored guests.

sentences.zh: 恆，安平人；

translations.literal: Heng was a man of Anping;
translations.idiomatic: Heng was from Anping;

sentences.zh: 琮，鑒之孫也。

translations.literal: Cong was the grandson of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was the grandson of Shi Jian.

sentences.zh: 廆以高瞻為將軍，瞻稱疾不就，廆數臨候之，撫其心曰：「君之疾在此，不在它也。

translations.literal: Hui made Gao Zhan a general; Zhan claimed illness and would not take office; Hui several times visited him in person, stroking his heart and saying: 'Your illness is here, not elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Hui offered Gao Zhan a general's commission, but Zhan pleaded illness and refused. Hui visited him repeatedly, laid a hand on his heart, and said, 'Your illness is here, not in your body.

sentences.zh: 今晉室喪亂，孤欲與諸君共清世難，翼戴帝室。

translations.literal: Now the house of Jin is in disorder; I wish to join with you gentlemen to clear the world's troubles and support the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Jin is in chaos. I wish to join with you in clearing the world's troubles and supporting the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 君中州望族，宜同斯願，奈何以華、夷之異，介然疏之哉！

translations.literal: You are a leading clan of the Central Plains and should share this wish—why, because of the difference between Chinese and barbarian, stand aloof in such a stiff and distant way!
translations.idiomatic: You are a leading family of the Central Plains and should share this ambition. Why let the distinction between Chinese and barbarian make you stand aloof!

sentences.zh: 夫立功立事，惟問志略何如耳，華、夷何足問乎！」

translations.literal: In establishing merit and achievement, one asks only what the will and plan are like—what is there to ask about Chinese and barbarian!'
translations.idiomatic: When a man sets out to achieve great things, what matters is the quality of his mind and plan—what does Chinese or barbarian matter!'

sentences.zh: 瞻猶不起，廆頗不平。

translations.literal: Zhan still would not rise to serve, and Hui was rather displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan still refused to serve, and Hui grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 龍驤主簿宋該，與瞻有隙，勸廆除之，廆不從。

translations.literal: Song Gai, Registrar of the Dragon Cavalry, who had a grudge against Zhan, urged Hui to eliminate him; Hui did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Song Gai, Registrar of the Dragon Cavalry, who bore a grudge against Zhan, urged Hui to kill him, but Hui refused.

sentences.zh: 瞻以憂卒。

translations.literal: Zhan died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan died of grief.

sentences.zh: 初，鞠羨既死，苟晞復以羨子彭為東萊太守。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Ju Xian had died, Gou Xi again made Xian's son Peng Administrator of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Ju Xian's death, Gou Xi had installed Xian's son Peng as Administrator of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 會曹嶷徇青州，與彭相攻；

translations.literal: When Cao Ni swept through Qingzhou he fought with Peng;
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Ni overran Qingzhou he clashed with Peng;

sentences.zh: 嶷兵雖強，郡人皆為彭死戰，嶷不能克。

translations.literal: though Ni's troops were strong, the people of the commandery all fought to the death for Peng, and Ni could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Ni's army was strong, but the people of the commandery fought to the death for Peng, and Ni could not break them.

sentences.zh: 久之，彭歎曰：「今天下大亂，強者為雄。

translations.literal: After a long time Peng sighed and said: 'Now the realm is in great disorder, and the strong become the heroes.
translations.idiomatic: After a long stalemate Peng sighed and said, 'The realm is in chaos, and the strong rule as they please.

sentences.zh: 曹亦鄉里，為天所相，苟可依憑，即為民主，何必與之力爭，使百姓肝腦塗地！

translations.literal: Cao is also a man of our home district, favored by Heaven; if we can rely on him he will be our lord—why must we struggle with him by force and make the common people bleed their livers and brains on the ground!
translations.idiomatic: Cao is a fellow townsman, clearly favored by Heaven. If we can rely on him, he will be our ruler. Why keep fighting until the people are slaughtered on every side!

sentences.zh: 吾去此，則禍自息矣。」

translations.literal: If I leave this place, the calamity will cease of itself.'
translations.idiomatic: If I leave, the killing will stop of its own accord.'

sentences.zh: 郡人以為不可，爭獻拒嶷之策，彭一無所用，與鄉里千餘家浮海歸崔毖。

translations.literal: The people of the commandery thought this impossible and vied to offer plans for resisting Ni; Peng used none of them, and with more than a thousand households of his home district crossed the sea to join Cui Bi.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the commandery protested and pressed plan after plan for resisting Ni, but Peng would hear none of them. With more than a thousand local households he took ship across the sea to join Cui Bi.

sentences.zh: 北海鄭林客於東萊，彭、嶷之相攻，林情無彼此。

translations.literal: Zheng Lin of Beihai was a guest in Donglai; when Peng and Ni attacked each other, Lin's feelings favored neither side.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Lin of Beihai was living in Donglai as a guest. When Peng and Ni fought, Lin took neither side.

sentences.zh: 嶷賢之，不敢侵掠，彭與之俱去。

translations.literal: Ni admired him and did not dare raid or plunder; Peng left together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ni admired him and left him unmolested, and Peng took Lin with him when he departed.

sentences.zh: 比至遼東，毖已敗，乃歸慕容廆。

translations.literal: By the time they reached Liaodong, Bi had already been defeated, and they then submitted to Murong Hui.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached Liaodong, Bi had already been defeated, and they went over to Murong Hui.

sentences.zh: 廆以彭參龍驤軍事。

translations.literal: Hui made Peng a staff officer of the Dragon Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Hui made Peng a staff officer on his Dragon Cavalry command.

sentences.zh: 遺鄭林車牛粟帛，皆不受，躬耕於野。

translations.literal: He sent Zheng Lin carts, oxen, grain, and silk, but Lin accepted none of them and farmed the fields himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hui sent Zheng Lin carts, oxen, grain, and silk, but Lin refused everything and farmed the fields with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 宋該勸廆獻捷江東，廆使該為表，裴嶷奉之，並所得三璽詣建康獻之。

translations.literal: Song Gai urged Hui to present a victory report to the region east of the Yangzi; Hui had Gai draft the memorial, Pei Yi bear it, and together with the three seals obtained, went to Jiankang to present them.
translations.idiomatic: Song Gai urged Hui to report his victory to the Jin court. Hui had Gai draft the memorial, Pei Yi carry it, and together with the three seals he had captured, sent them to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 高句麗數寇遼東，廆遣慕容翰、慕容仕伐之；

translations.literal: Koguryo repeatedly raided Liaodong; Hui sent Murong Han and Murong Shi to attack them;
translations.idiomatic: Koguryo raided Liaodong repeatedly, and Hui sent Murong Han and Murong Shi against them;

sentences.zh: 高句麗王乙弗利逆來求盟，翰、仁乃還。

translations.literal: the King of Koguryo Yifuli came in person to seek alliance, and Han and Ren then returned.
translations.idiomatic: the Koguryo king Yifuli came in person to sue for peace, and Han and Ren withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是歲，蒲洪降趙，趙主曜以洪為率義侯。

translations.literal: That year, Pu Hong submitted to Zhao, and the Zhao ruler Liu Yao made Hong Marquis Who Leads Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: That year Pu Hong submitted to Zhao, and Liu Yao enfeoffed him as Marquis Who Leads Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 屠各路松多起兵於新平、扶風以附晉王保，保使其將楊曼、王連據陳倉，張顗、周庸據陰密，路松多據草壁，秦隴氐、羌多應之。

translations.literal: Tulu Songqi raised troops in Xinping and Fufeng to join Prince Bao of Jin; Bao had his generals Yang Man and Wang Lian hold Chencang, Zhang Yi and Zhou Yong hold Yinmi, and Songduo hold Caobi; many Di and Qiang of Qin and Long responded.
translations.idiomatic: Tulu Songduo raised troops in Xinping and Fufeng to join Prince Bao of Jin. Bao posted Yang Man and Wang Lian at Chencang, Zhang Yi and Zhou Yong at Yinmi, and Songduo at Caobi, and many Di and Qiang of Qin and Long rose in support.

sentences.zh: 趙主曜遣諸將攻之，不克；

translations.literal: the Zhao ruler Liu Yao sent generals to attack them but could not overcome them;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao sent generals against them but could not break them;

sentences.zh: 曜自將擊之。

translations.literal: Yao led the attack in person.
translations.idiomatic: so Yao marched out in person.

sentences.zh: 中宗元皇帝中太興三年（

translations.literal: Third year of Taixing in the middle reign of Emperor Yuan of the Zhongzong line (
translations.idiomatic: The third year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan of Jin (

sentences.zh: 庚辰，公元三二零年）

translations.literal: gengchen, the year 320 CE)
translations.idiomatic: gengchen, 320 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，曜攻陳倉，王連戰死，楊曼奔南氐。

translations.literal: Spring, first month: Yao attacked Chencang; Wang Lian died in battle and Yang Man fled to the Southern Di.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Yao attacked Chencang. Wang Lian was killed in battle and Yang Man fled to the Southern Di.

sentences.zh: 曜進拔草壁，路松多奔隴城；

translations.literal: Yao advanced and took Caobi; Songduo fled to Longcheng;
translations.idiomatic: Yao advanced and took Caobi; Songduo fled to Longcheng;

sentences.zh: 又拔陰密。

translations.literal: he also took Yinmi.
translations.idiomatic: and also captured Yinmi.

sentences.zh: 晉王保懼，遷於桑城。

translations.literal: Prince Bao of Jin was afraid and moved to Sangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Bao, alarmed, withdrew to Sangcheng.

sentences.zh: 曜還長安，以劉雅為大司徒。

translations.literal: Yao returned to Chang'an and made Liu Ya Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Yao returned to Chang'an and appointed Liu Ya Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 張春謀奉晉王保奔涼州，張遣其將陰監將兵迎之，聲言翼衛，其實拒之。

translations.literal: Zhang Chun plotted to escort Prince Bao of Jin to Liangzhou; Zhang Shi sent his general Yin Jian with troops to welcome him, claiming to support and guard him but in fact blocking him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun plotted to escort Prince Bao to Liangzhou. Zhang Shi sent his general Yin Jian with troops to meet him, claiming to escort him but in fact to block him.

sentences.zh: 段末柸攻段匹磾，破之。

translations.literal: Duan Moleng attacked Duan Pidi and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Moleng attacked Duan Pidi and routed him.

sentences.zh: 匹磾謂邵續曰：「吾本夷狄，以慕義破家。

translations.literal: Pidi said to Shao Xu: 'I was originally a barbarian of the Yi and Di, who ruined my house through admiration of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Pidi said to Shao Xu, 'I am a barbarian by birth who ruined my house through devotion to righteousness.

sentences.zh: 君不忘久要，請相與共擊末柸。」

translations.literal: You have not forgotten our long-standing bond—please join with me in attacking Moleng.'
translations.idiomatic: You have not forgotten our old bond. Join me in striking Moleng.'

sentences.zh: 續許之。

translations.literal: Xu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂相與追擊末杯，大破之。

translations.literal: They then pursued and attacked Moleng together and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Together they pursued Moleng and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 匹磾與弟文鴦攻薊。

translations.literal: Pidi and his brother Wenyang attacked Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Pidi and his brother Wenyang besieged Ji.

sentences.zh: 後趙王勒知續勢孤，遣中山公虎將兵圍厭次，孫萇攻續別營十一，皆下之。

translations.literal: The Later Zhao King Shi Le, knowing Xu was isolated in strength, sent Duke of Zhongshan Hu with troops to besiege Yanci; Sun Chang attacked eleven of Xu's detached camps and took them all.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le of Later Zhao, seeing that Xu stood alone, sent the Duke of Zhongshan, Shi Hu, to besiege Yanci while Sun Chang overran eleven of Xu's outlying camps.

sentences.zh: 二月，續自出擊虎，虎伏騎斷其後，遂執續，使降其城。

translations.literal: Second month: Xu came out in person to attack Hu; Hu's hidden horsemen cut off his rear, seized Xu, and made him order the city to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Xu marched out in person against Hu. Hu's hidden cavalry cut off his retreat, captured him, and forced him to order his city to surrender.

sentences.zh: 續呼兄子竺等謂曰：「吾志欲報國，不幸至此。

translations.literal: Xu called his brother's sons Zhu and the others and said to them: "My ambition was to serve the state; unfortunately I have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Xu summoned his brother's sons Zhu and the others and said, "I meant to serve the realm; fate has brought me to this pass.

sentences.zh: 汝等努力奉匹磾為主，勿有貳心！」

translations.literal: You must exert yourselves to support Pidi as your leader—harbor no divided loyalty!"
translations.idiomatic: Do your utmost to serve Pidi as your master. Let there be no second loyalty."

sentences.zh: 匹磾自薊還，未至厭次，聞續已沒，眾懼而散，復為虎所遮。

translations.literal: Pidi was returning from Ji when, before reaching Yanci, he heard that Xu had perished; the troops, afraid, scattered, and were again blocked by Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Pidi was marching back from Ji. Before he reached Yanci he learned that Xu was dead. His men panicked and broke ranks, only to be intercepted again by Hu.

sentences.zh: 文鴦以親兵數百力戰，始得入城，與續子緝、兄子存、竺等嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Wenyang fought fiercely with several hundred personal troops before he could enter the city; with Xu's son Ji, his brother's son Cun, Zhu, and the others he defended the walls stubbornly.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyang battled with a few hundred handpicked troops before forcing his way into the city. There he joined Xu's son Ji, his nephew Cun, Zhu, and the others in a desperate defense of the walls.

sentences.zh: 虎送續於襄國，勒以為忠，釋而禮之，以為從事中郎。

translations.literal: Hu sent Xu to Xiangguo; Le considered him loyal, released him and treated him with ceremony, and made him Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Hu sent Xu to Xiangguo. Le judged him a man of loyalty, freed him with full honors, and appointed him Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 因下令：「自今克敵，獲士人，毋得擅殺，必生致之。」

translations.literal: He then issued an order: "From now on, when enemies are defeated and men of learning captured, none may be killed on his own authority—they must be brought in alive."
translations.idiomatic: Le then issued an order: "Henceforth, when you defeat the enemy and capture scholarly men, you must not kill them on your own authority. Bring them in alive."

sentences.zh: 吏部郎劉胤聞續被攻，言於帝曰：「北方籓鎮盡矣，惟餘邵續而已；

translations.literal: Liu Yin, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, hearing that Xu was under attack, said to the Emperor: "The northern frontier garrisons are all gone—only Shao Xu remains;
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yin, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, heard that Xu was under attack, he told the Emperor, "The northern frontier holds are all lost. Only Shao Xu is left.

sentences.zh: 如使復為石虎所滅，孤義士之心，阻歸本之路。

translations.literal: If he is again destroyed by Shi Hu, the hearts of loyal men will be isolated and the road home barred.
translations.idiomatic: If Shi Hu wipes him out, men of loyal purpose will stand alone and the path back to the homeland will be cut off.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜發兵救之。」

translations.literal: I humbly suggest that troops should be sent to rescue him."
translations.idiomatic: I believe we should send troops to his relief."

sentences.zh: 帝不能從。

translations.literal: The Emperor could not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor refused to act on it.

sentences.zh: 聞續已沒，乃下詔以續位任授其子緝。

translations.literal: On hearing that Xu had perished, an edict was issued conferring Xu's rank and office on his son Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Xu was dead, the court issued an edict granting his son Ji his rank and post.

sentences.zh: 趙將尹安、宋始、宋恕、趙慎四軍屯洛陽，叛，降後趙。

translations.literal: The four Zhao armies of Yin An, Song Shi, Song Shu, and Zhao Shen stationed at Luoyang rebelled and surrendered to Later Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Four Later Han armies under Yin An, Song Shi, Song Shu, and Zhao Shen garrisoned at Luoyang rebelled and went over to Later Zhao.

sentences.zh: 後趙將石生引兵赴之；

translations.literal: Later Zhao's general Shi Sheng led troops to go there;
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao sent General Shi Sheng with troops to take possession;

sentences.zh: 安等復叛，降司州刺史李矩。

translations.literal: An and the others rebelled again and surrendered to Li Ju, Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: An and his officers switched sides again and submitted to Li Ju, Inspector of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 矩使穎川太守郭默將兵入洛。

translations.literal: Ju sent Yingchuan Administrator Guo Mo with troops to enter Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju sent Guo Mo, Administrator of Yingchuan, to march into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 石生虜宋始一軍，北渡河。

translations.literal: Shi Sheng captured Song Shi's army and crossed the Yellow River northward.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng seized Song Shi's force and retreated north across the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 於是河南之民皆相帥歸矩，洛陽遂空。

translations.literal: Thereupon the people south of the river all led one another back to Ju, and Luoyang was left empty.
translations.idiomatic: The populace south of the river followed one another to Li Ju's banner, and Luoyang was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 三月，裴嶷至建康，盛稱慕容廆之威德，賢俊皆為之用，朝廷始重之。

translations.literal: Third month: Pei Yi reached Jiankang and spoke at length of Murong Hui's power and virtue, how worthy men all served him; the court began to hold him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Pei Yi arrived at Jiankang and praised Murong Hui's authority and virtue at length, noting that talented men flocked to his service. The court began to take him seriously.

sentences.zh: 帝謂嶷曰：「卿中朝名臣，當留江東，朕別詔龍驤送卿家屬。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Yi: "You are a celebrated minister of the central court—you should remain in the southeast. I shall separately order Dragon-Courser to escort your family here."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Yi, "You are a distinguished minister of the central court and ought to stay in the southeast. I will issue a separate order for Dragon-Courser to bring your family to join you."

sentences.zh: 嶷曰：「臣少蒙國恩，出入省闥，若得復奉輦轂，臣之至榮。

translations.literal: Yi said: "From youth I have received the state's grace and passed in and out of the imperial precincts; if I could again attend the imperial carriage, that would be my supreme honor.
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied, "I received the court's favor in my youth and walked the halls of power. To serve again at the emperor's side would be the greatest honor I could wish for.

sentences.zh: 但以舊京淪沒，山陵穿毀，雖名臣宿將，莫能雪恥，獨慕容龍驤竭忠王室，志除凶逆，故使臣萬里歸誠。

translations.literal: Yet since the old capital fell, the imperial tombs were violated and ruined, and though famous ministers and veteran generals could not wash away the shame, only Dragon-Courser Murong has exhausted his loyalty to the royal house and resolved to destroy the wicked; therefore he sent me ten thousand li to declare devotion.
translations.idiomatic: But the old capital has fallen, the imperial tombs lie desecrated, and even famous ministers and seasoned generals have failed to redeem that shame. Only Murong Dragon-Courser has served the throne with tireless loyalty and vowed to destroy the usurpers. That is why he sent me across a thousand miles to pledge our devotion.

sentences.zh: 今臣來而不返，必謂朝廷以其僻陋而棄之，孤其向義之心，使懈體於討賊，此臣之所甚惜，是以不敢徇私而忘公也。」

translations.literal: If I come and do not return, it will surely be thought the court has cast him off for remoteness and rusticity, isolating his loyal heart and slackening his effort against the rebels—this is what I deeply regret, and therefore I dare not favor private feeling over public duty."
translations.idiomatic: If I stay here and do not return, men will say the court has cast him aside because he is remote and unsophisticated. That would chill his loyal resolve and weaken his campaign against the rebels. I cannot bear that, and so I dare not let private comfort override public duty."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿言是也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Your words are right."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "You speak truly."

sentences.zh: 乃遣使隨嶷拜廆安北將軍、平州刺史。

translations.literal: An envoy was then sent with Yi to invest Hui as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent an envoy with Yi to appoint Hui General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 閏月，以周顗為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month Zhou Yi was made Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Zhou Yi was appointed Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 晉王保將張春、楊次與別將楊韜不協，勸保誅之，且請擊陳安；

translations.literal: Prince Bao of Jin's generals Zhang Chun and Yang Ci were at odds with the separate commander Yang Tao; they urged Bao to execute them and also requested an attack on Chen An;
translations.idiomatic: Among Prince Bao's generals, Zhang Chun and Yang Ci feuded with the detached commander Yang Tao. They urged Bao to execute the two men and proposed an assault on Chen An.

sentences.zh: 保皆不從。

translations.literal: Bao would not heed any of this.
translations.idiomatic: Bao refused both requests.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，春，次幽保，殺之。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month: Chun and Ci plotted against Bao and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, Zhang Chun and Yang Ci conspired against Bao and murdered him.

sentences.zh: 保體肥大，重八百斤，喜睡，好讀書，而闇弱無斷，故及於難。

translations.literal: Bao's body was large and stout, weighing eight hundred jin; he loved sleep and loved reading, yet was dim-witted, weak, and without resolve—therefore he met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was enormously corpulent—eight hundred jin—and fond of sleep and books, but he was indecisive and weak of will. That is how he came to such an end.

sentences.zh: 保無子，張春立宗室子瞻為世子，稱大將軍。

translations.literal: Bao had no son; Zhang Chun set up a clansman, Zhan, as heir apparent and styled himself Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Bao left no son. Zhang Chun installed a royal clansman named Zhan as heir apparent and took the title Grand General for himself.

sentences.zh: 保眾散，奔涼州者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Bao's forces scattered; more than ten thousand fled to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's followers broke apart, and more than ten thousand fled toward Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 陳安表於趙主曜，請討瞻等。

translations.literal: Chen An memorialized the Zhao ruler Liu Yao, requesting permission to attack Zhan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An petitioned Liu Yao, ruler of Zhao, asking leave to attack Zhan and his party.

sentences.zh: 曜以安為大將軍，擊瞻，殺之；

translations.literal: Yao made An Grand General, attacked Zhan, and killed him;
translations.idiomatic: Yao appointed Chen An Grand General and sent him against Zhan, who was killed in the fighting;

sentences.zh: 張春奔枹罕。

translations.literal: Zhang Chun fled away to Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun escaped to Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 安執楊次，於保柩前斬之，因以祭保。

translations.literal: An seized Yang Ci and beheaded him before Bao's coffin, using this to sacrifice to Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An seized Yang Ci and executed him before Bao's coffin as a sacrifice to the dead prince.

sentences.zh: 安以天子禮葬保於上邽，謚曰元王。

translations.literal: An buried Bao at Shanggui with the rites due an emperor and gave him the posthumous title Prince Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An buried Bao at Shanggui with imperial ceremony and posthumously titled him Prince Yuan.

sentences.zh: 羊鑒討徐龕，頓兵下邳，不敢前。

translations.literal: Yang Jian campaigned against Xu Kan but halted his troops at Xiapi and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian marched against Xu Kan but halted at Xiapi, unwilling to press forward.

sentences.zh: 蔡豹敗龕於檀丘，龕求救於後趙。

translations.literal: Cai Bao defeated Kan at Tanqiu; Kan requested aid from Later Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Bao routed Xu Kan at Tanqiu, and Kan appealed to Later Zhao for help.

sentences.zh: 後趙王勒遣其將王伏都救之，又使張敬將兵為之後繼。

translations.literal: Later Zhao's King Le sent his general Wang Fudu to rescue him, and also dispatched Zhang Jing with troops as reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: King Le of Later Zhao sent his general Wang Fudu to the rescue and ordered Zhang Jing to follow with supporting troops.

sentences.zh: 勒多所邀求，而伏都淫暴，龕患之。

translations.literal: Le made many demands, and Fudu was lewd and violent—Kan resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Le piled up one demand after another, and Wang Fudu was brutal and debauched. Xu Kan came to loathe them.

sentences.zh: 張敬至東平，龕疑其襲己，乃斬伏都等三百餘人，復來請降。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jing reached Dongping, Kan suspected he meant to attack him; he then beheaded Fudu and more than three hundred others and again came to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jing reached Dongping, Xu Kan feared a surprise attack. He slaughtered Wang Fudu and more than three hundred of his men and once again offered to surrender to Jin.

sentences.zh: 勒大怒，命張敬據險以守之。

translations.literal: Le was greatly angered and ordered Zhang Jing to hold fortified positions against him.
translations.idiomatic: Le was furious and ordered Zhang Jing to seize strongpoints and hold the line against him.

sentences.zh: 帝亦惡龕反覆，不受其降，敕鑒、豹以時進討。

translations.literal: The Emperor also despised Kan's flip-flopping and would not accept his surrender; he ordered Jian and Bao to advance and attack on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor likewise distrusted Kan's chronic double-dealing and rejected his surrender, ordering Yang Jian and Cai Bao to press the attack without delay.

sentences.zh: 鑒猶疑憚不進，尚書令刁協劾奏鑒，免死除名，以蔡豹代領其兵。

translations.literal: Jian still hesitated and dared not advance; Minister of the Imperial Secretariat Diao Xie memorialized against him; he was spared death but removed from the rolls, and Cai Bao was put in command of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian still hung back in fear. Minister of the Imperial Secretariat Diao Xie impeached him. He was spared execution but stripped of rank, and Cai Bao took over his command.

sentences.zh: 王導以所舉失人，乞自貶，帝不許。

translations.literal: Wang Dao, because his recommendation had proved wrong, asked to demote himself; the Emperor would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao had recommended Yang Jian and asked to be demoted when the appointment failed. The Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 六月，後趙孔萇攻段匹磾，恃勝而不設備，段文鴦襲擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Later Zhao's Kong Chang attacked Duan Pidi; trusting in victory he made no preparations, and Duan Wenyang struck in surprise and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Kong Chang of Later Zhao attacked Duan Pidi. Overconfident after earlier victories, he left his camp unprepared. Duan Wenyang caught him off guard and crushed his army.

sentences.zh: 京兆人劉弘客居涼州天梯山，以妖術惑眾，從受道者千餘人，西平元公張寔左右皆事之。

translations.literal: Liu Hong of Jingzhao, dwelling at Tianti Mountain in Liangzhou, beguiled the masses with sorcery; more than a thousand became his disciples, and all around Zhang Shi, Duke of Xiping, served him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong of Jingzhao lived as a guest on Tianti Mountain in Liangzhou and won followers with occult arts. More than a thousand took him as teacher, and even the attendants of Zhang Shi, Duke of Xiping, fell under his sway.

sentences.zh: 帳下閻涉、牙門趙卬，皆弘鄉人，弘謂之曰：「天與我神璽，應王涼州。」

translations.literal: Yan She of his staff and Zhao Ang of the gate guard, both fellow townsmen of Hong, Hong said to them: "Heaven has given me a divine seal—I am destined to rule Liangzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Yan She of his household staff and Zhao Ang of the gate guard were both Hong's countrymen. Hong told them, "Heaven has granted me a divine seal. I am fated to reign over Liangzhou."

sentences.zh: 涉、卬信之，密與寔左右十餘人謀殺寔，奉弘為主。

translations.literal: She and Ang believed him; secretly with more than ten of Shi's attendants they plotted to kill Shi and install Hong as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: She and Ang believed him. Secretly they joined more than ten of Shi's attendants in a plot to murder Shi and enthrone Hong.

sentences.zh: 寔弟茂知其謀，請誅弘。

translations.literal: Shi's brother Mao learned of the plot and requested that Hong be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's brother Mao uncovered the plot and urged that Hong be put to death.

sentences.zh: 寔令牙門將史初收之，未至，涉等懷刃而入，殺寔於外寢。

translations.literal: Shi ordered the gate general Shi Chu to seize him, but before he arrived She and the others entered with blades hidden and killed Shi in the outer chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Shi ordered Gate General Shi Chu to arrest him. Before Chu could arrive, She and the others slipped in with concealed blades and murdered Shi in his outer chamber.

sentences.zh: 弘見史初至，謂曰：「使君已死，殺我何為！」

translations.literal: When Hong saw Chu arrive he said: "The lord is already dead—what purpose is served by killing me!"
translations.idiomatic: When Hong saw Chu arriving, he cried, "Your master is already dead—what good will killing me do?"

sentences.zh: 初怒，截其舌而囚之，轘於姑臧市，誅其黨與數百人。

translations.literal: Chu, enraged, cut out his tongue and imprisoned him; he was torn apart at the marketplace of Guzang, and several hundred of his accomplices were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Chu cut out his tongue and threw him in prison. Hong was dismembered in the Guzang marketplace, and several hundred of his followers were put to death.

sentences.zh: 左司馬陰元等以寔子駿尚幼，推張茂為涼州刺史、西平公，赦其境內，以駿為撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: Left Major Yin Yuan and others, because Shi's son Jun was still young, set up Zhang Mao as Inspector of Liangzhou and Duke of Xiping, amnestied all within the territory, and made Jun General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Left Major Yin Yuan and his colleagues, finding Shi's son Jun still a child, installed Zhang Mao as Inspector of Liangzhou and Duke of Xiping, declared a general amnesty, and appointed Jun General Who Pacifies the Army.
