sentences.zh: 丙辰，趙將解虎及長水校尉尹車謀反，與巴酋句徐、庫彭等相結；

translations.literal: On bingchen, Zhao generals Xie Hu and Chief Commandant of the Changshui Guard Yin Che plotted rebellion, joining with Ba chieftains Xu Gou and Ku Peng and others;
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingchen, Zhao generals Xie Hu and Chief Commandant Yin Che of the Changshui Guard plotted rebellion in league with the Ba chieftains Xu Gou and Ku Peng.

sentences.zh: 事覺，虎、車皆伏誅。

translations.literal: The affair was discovered; Hu and Che were both executed.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was exposed. Both Hu and Che were put to death.

sentences.zh: 趙主曜囚徐、彭等五十餘人於阿房，將殺之；

translations.literal: Zhao ruler Yao imprisoned Xu, Peng, and more than fifty others at Epang and was about to kill them;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao imprisoned Xu, Peng, and more than fifty others at Epang and prepared to execute them.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫遊子遠諫曰：「聖王用刑，惟誅元惡而已，不宜多殺。」

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Youzi Yuan remonstrated: "When a sage king punishes, he executes only the chief culprits—not many should be killed."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Youzi Yuan remonstrated, "A sage ruler uses punishment to destroy the ringleaders alone. Mass killing is not warranted."

sentences.zh: 爭之，叩頭流血。

translations.literal: He argued fiercely, banging his head until it bled.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed his case until his forehead streamed blood from repeated kowtows.

sentences.zh: 曜怒，以為助逆而囚之；

translations.literal: Yao was angry, deemed him an accomplice to rebellion, and imprisoned him;
translations.idiomatic: Yao flew into a rage, accused him of abetting the rebels, and had him thrown into prison;

sentences.zh: 盡殺徐、彭等，屍諸市十日，乃投於水。

translations.literal: he killed Xu, Peng, and all the rest; their bodies were displayed in the market ten days, then thrown into the water.
translations.idiomatic: then killed Xu, Peng, and all the rest. Their corpses hung in the marketplace for ten days before being dumped in the river.

sentences.zh: 於是巴眾盡反，推巴酋句渠知為主，自稱大秦，改元曰平趙。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the Ba people rebelled, set up the Ba chieftain Qu Zhizhi as leader, styled themselves Great Qin, and changed the era name to Ping Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: The entire Ba population rose in revolt, proclaiming the Ba chieftain Qu Zhizhi their leader. They styled their regime Great Qin and adopted the era name Ping Zhao.

sentences.zh: 四山氐、羌、巴、羯應之者三十餘萬，關中大亂，城門晝閉。

translations.literal: Di, Qiang, Ba, and Jie from the four mountains who answered the call numbered more than three hundred thousand; Guanzhong fell into great chaos and the city gates were closed by day.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred thousand Di, Qiang, Ba, and Jie from the surrounding hills joined them. Guanzhong plunged into chaos, and the city gates were barred even in daylight.

sentences.zh: 子遠又從獄中上表諫爭，曜手毀其表曰：「大荔奴，不憂命在須臾，猶敢如此，嫌死晚邪！」

translations.literal: Yuan again from prison submitted a memorial of remonstrance; Yao tore it apart with his hand and said: "You great Li slave—you do not worry that your life hangs by a moment, yet still dare act thus—do you think you will die too late!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan submitted another memorial of protest from his cell. Yao tore it to pieces and snarled, "You Li slave! Your life hangs by a thread and you still dare this—is death coming too slowly for you?"

sentences.zh: 叱左右速殺之。

translations.literal: He shouted to those beside him to kill him at once.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his attendants to kill him immediately.

sentences.zh: 中山王雅、郭汜、朱紀、呼延晏等諫曰：「子遠幽囚，禍在不測，猶不忘諫爭，忠之至也。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhongshan Ya, Guo Si, Zhu Ji, Huyan Yan, and others remonstrated: "Yuan is confined in darkness, disaster hovering over him unknown, yet he does not forget remonstrance—loyalty at its utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhongshan Ya, Guo Si, Zhu Ji, Huyan Yan, and others pleaded, "Yuan lies in prison facing unknown peril, yet he never ceases to counsel you—that is loyalty in its purest form.

sentences.zh: 陛下縱不能用，奈何殺之！

translations.literal: Your Majesty may not adopt his counsel—how can you kill him!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty may reject his advice, but how can you put him to death?

sentences.zh: 若子遠朝誅，臣等亦當夕死，以彰陛下之過，天下將皆捨陛下而去，陛下誰與居乎！」

translations.literal: If Yuan is executed in the morning, we too shall die by evening, to expose Your Majesty's fault—the realm will all abandon Your Majesty and go; with whom will Your Majesty dwell then!"
translations.idiomatic: Execute Yuan in the morning and you will see us dead by evening—a public witness to your error. The realm will abandon you. Then whom will you rule?"

sentences.zh: 曜意解，乃赦之。

translations.literal: Yao's mood eased, and he pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's anger cooled, and he spared Yuan's life.

sentences.zh: 曜敕內外戒嚴，將自討渠知。

translations.literal: Yao ordered strict security within and without and intended to campaign in person against Zhizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao put the capital under martial law and prepared to lead the campaign against Qu Zhizhi himself.

sentences.zh: 子遠又諫曰：「陛下誠能用臣策，一月可定，大駕不必親征也。」

translations.literal: Yuan again remonstrated: "If Your Majesty will truly employ my plan, it can be settled in one month—the imperial carriage need not go out in person."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan remonstrated again: "If Your Majesty adopts my plan, the rebellion can be crushed within a month. There is no need for you to take the field personally."

sentences.zh: 曜曰：「卿試言之。」

translations.literal: Yao said: "Try stating it."
translations.idiomatic: Yao said, "Tell me your plan."

sentences.zh: 子遠曰：「彼非有大志，欲圖非望也，直畏陛下威刑，欲逃死耳。

translations.literal: Yuan said: "They have no great ambition or desire for unlawful elevation—they simply fear Your Majesty's stern punishment and wish to flee death.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan replied, "These rebels have no grand ambition or claim to the throne. They rose because they feared your harsh punishments and hoped only to escape death.

sentences.zh: 陛下莫若廊然大赦，與之更始；

translations.literal: Your Majesty should simply issue a sweeping amnesty and give them a fresh start;
translations.idiomatic: Issue a sweeping amnesty and offer them a new beginning;

sentences.zh: 應前日坐虎、車等事，其家老弱沒入奚官者，皆縱遣之，使之自相招引，聽其復業。

translations.literal: for those implicated in the affair of Hu, Che, and the like whose elderly and weak kin were confiscated into palace service, release them all, let them summon one another home, and allow them to resume their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Release the families of those implicated in the Xie Hu and Yin Che affair—every elderly relative and child seized for palace labor—and let them call their kin home and return to their trades.

sentences.zh: 彼既得生路，何為不降！

translations.literal: Once they have a path to life, why would they not surrender!
translations.idiomatic: Give them a way to live and they will lay down their arms.

sentences.zh: 若其中自知罪重，屯結不散者，願假臣弱兵五千，必為陛下梟之。

translations.literal: If among them some know their guilt is grave and hold together refusing to disperse, I ask only five thousand weak troops—I will surely present their heads to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: If any holdouts know their guilt is too heavy to disband, lend me five thousand second-rate troops and I will deliver their heads to you.

sentences.zh: 不然，今反者彌山被谷，雖以天威臨之，恐非歲月可除也。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, rebels now fill mountains and cover valleys; though Your Majesty's august might presses down on them, I fear it cannot be extinguished in months."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the rebels cover every hill and valley. Even with the full weight of imperial power, this will not be over in months."

sentences.zh: 曜大悅，即日大赦，以子遠為車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、都督雍、秦征討諸軍事。

translations.literal: Yao was greatly pleased, proclaimed a general amnesty that very day, and made Yuan General of Chariots and Cavalry, with dignities equal to the Three Excellencies, and Supervisor of military affairs for the pacification of Yong and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was delighted. That same day he declared a general amnesty and appointed Yuan General of Chariots and Cavalry with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, putting him in overall command of the Yong and Qin pacification.

sentences.zh: 子遠屯於雍城，降者十餘萬；

translations.literal: Yuan encamped at Yongcheng; more than one hundred thousand surrendered;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan encamped at Yongcheng and received the surrender of more than one hundred thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 移軍安定，反者皆降。

translations.literal: he shifted his army to Anding, and the rebels all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When he moved on to Anding, the remaining rebels submitted as well.

sentences.zh: 惟句氏宗黨五千餘家保於陰密，進攻，滅之，遂引兵巡隴右。

translations.literal: Only more than five thousand households of the Qu clan's faction held out at Yinmi; he attacked, destroyed them, and then led his troops on a tour of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Only some five thousand households of the Qu clan held out at Yinmi. Yuan attacked and annihilated them, then marched through Longyou.

sentences.zh: 先是氐、羌十餘萬落據險不服，其酋虛除權渠自號秦王。

translations.literal: Earlier, more than one hundred thousand Di and Qiang encampments held the passes and would not submit; their chieftain Xuchu Ququ styled himself King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, more than one hundred thousand Di and Qiang encampments had seized the high passes and refused submission. Their chieftain Xuchu Ququ proclaimed himself King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 子遠進造其壁，權渠出兵拒之，五戰皆敗。

translations.literal: Yuan advanced to his ramparts; Ququ sent troops to resist him and was defeated in five engagements.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan marched on his stronghold. Ququ met him in the field and lost five battles in succession.

sentences.zh: 權渠欲降，其子伊餘大言於眾曰：「往者劉曜自來，猶無若我何，況此偏師，何謂降也！」

translations.literal: Ququ wished to surrender, but his son Yiyu boldly told the assembly: "In the past when Liu Yao came in person he still could do nothing to us—how much less this detached division! Why speak of surrender!"
translations.idiomatic: Ququ wanted to surrender, but his son Yiyu harangued the troops: "When Liu Yao came in person he could not break us—what threat is this scratch force? Surrender is out of the question!"

sentences.zh: 帥勁卒五萬，晨壓子遠壘門。

translations.literal: He led fifty thousand picked troops and at dawn pressed against Yuan's camp gate.
translations.idiomatic: He led fifty thousand elite troops and at daybreak stormed Yuan's camp gates.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲擊之，子遠曰：「伊餘勇悍，當今無敵，所將之兵，復精於我。

translations.literal: The generals wished to strike; Yuan said: "Yiyu is fierce and bold, unmatched today, and the troops he leads are finer than ours.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's officers wanted to give battle. He said, "Yiyu is the fiercest fighter alive, and his troops outmatch ours in training.

sentences.zh: 又其父新敗，怒氣方盛，其鋒不可當也，不如緩之，使氣竭而後擊之。」

translations.literal: Moreover his father has just been defeated and his rage is at its height—their edge cannot be met; better to delay until their spirit is exhausted and then strike."
translations.idiomatic: His father has just suffered defeat, so Yiyu's fury is at its peak. We cannot meet that charge head-on. Let them wear themselves out, then strike."

sentences.zh: 乃堅壁不戰。

translations.literal: He then held the walls and would not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan ordered his men to hold the fortifications and refuse battle.

sentences.zh: 伊餘有驕色，子遠伺其無備，夜，勒兵蓐食，旦，值大風塵昏，子遠悉眾出掩之，生擒伊餘，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: Yiyu wore a look of arrogance; Yuan watched for his lapse in preparedness—at night he ordered the troops to eat in their bedrolls; at dawn, when a great wind raised dust and dimmed the light, Yuan sent his entire force out in a surprise attack, captured Yiyu alive, and took all his troops prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyu grew overconfident. Yuan watched for his opening. That night he had his men eat beside their bedrolls. At dawn a sandstorm blew in. Yuan led his full force in a surprise attack, captured Yiyu alive, and took every one of his soldiers prisoner.

sentences.zh: 權渠大懼，被發、剺面請降。

translations.literal: Ququ was greatly afraid; with hair disheveled and face slashed he requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Ququ was terrified. With his hair loose and his face cut in mourning, he begged to surrender.

sentences.zh: 子遠啟曜，以權渠為征西將軍、西戎公，分徙伊餘兄弟及其部落二十餘萬口於長安。

translations.literal: Yuan reported to Yao and made Ququ General Who Conquers the West and Duke of Xirong; he resettled Yiyu's brothers and their tribes—more than two hundred thousand souls—to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan reported to Yao, confirmed Ququ as General Who Conquers the West and Duke of Xirong, and relocated Yiyu's brothers and their tribes—more than two hundred thousand people—to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 曜以子遠為大司徒、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Yao made Yuan Grand Minister of Education and Director of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao appointed Yuan Grand Minister of Education with oversight of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 曜立太學，選民之神志可教者千五百人，擇儒臣以教之。

translations.literal: Yao established the Imperial Academy, selecting fifteen hundred common people whose minds and spirits were teachable, and chose Confucian officials to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Yao founded an imperial academy, enrolled fifteen hundred subjects judged fit for instruction, and assigned Confucian scholars to teach them.

sentences.zh: 作酆明觀及西宮，起陵霄台於滈池，又於霸陵西南營壽陵。

translations.literal: He built the Fengming Observatory and the Western Palace, raised the Lingxiao Terrace at the Hao Pool, and also constructed the Shou Mausoleum southwest of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Fengming Observatory and the Western Palace, raised the Lingxiao Terrace beside the Hao Pool, and began work on the Shou Mausoleum southwest of Baling.

sentences.zh: 侍中喬豫、和苞上疏諫，以為：「衛文公承亂亡之後，節用愛民，營建宮室，得其時制，故能興康叔之業，延九百之祚。

translations.literal: Attendants-in-Ordinary Qiao Yu and He Bao submitted a memorial of remonstrance, holding: "Duke Wen of Wei, inheriting after chaos and extinction, was frugal and loved the people; in building palaces he kept to timely measure, and therefore was able to revive the enterprise of Duke Kang and extend the nine hundred years of fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants-in-Ordinary Qiao Yu and He Bao submitted a memorial protesting the construction. They argued, "Duke Wen of Wei inherited a realm devastated by chaos. He was frugal, cared for his people, and built palaces only to proper scale—and so revived the legacy of Duke Kang and preserved the Zhou for nine hundred years.

sentences.zh: 前奉詔書營酆明觀，市道細民鹹譏其奢曰：『以一觀之功，足以平涼州矣！』

translations.literal: Earlier, when the edict was received to build the Fengming Observatory, petty folk in the marketplace all mocked its extravagance, saying: 'The cost of one observatory would be enough to pacify Liangzhou!
translations.idiomatic: When you ordered the Fengming Observatory built, common people in the markets mocked the extravagance, saying, 'What that one building cost could have pacified all of Liangzhou!

sentences.zh: 今又欲擬阿房而建西宮，法瓊台而起陵霄，其為勞費，億萬酆明；

translations.literal: Now you wish to model the Western Palace on Epang and the Lingxiao Terrace on the Jade Tower—the labor and expense will be tens of millions of Fengmings;
translations.idiomatic: Now you propose a Western Palace to rival Epang and a Lingxiao Terrace modeled on the Jade Tower of old. The labor and expense will dwarf the Fengming Observatory ten thousand times over;

sentences.zh: 若以資軍旅，乃可兼吳、蜀而壹齊、魏矣！

translations.literal: if applied to the army, one could subdue Wu and Shu together and unify Qi and Wei!
translations.idiomatic: Spend that treasure on the army and you could conquer Wu and Shu in one stroke and unite the lands of Qi and Wei!

sentences.zh: 又聞營建壽陵，周圍四里，深三十五丈，以銅為槨，飾以黃金；

translations.literal: We also hear that the Shou Mausoleum is being built, four li in circumference, thirty-five zhang deep, with copper for the outer coffin and gold for ornamentation;
translations.idiomatic: We also hear you are building the Shou Mausoleum—four li around, thirty-five zhang deep, with a copper coffin chamber and gold adornments;

sentences.zh: 功費若此，殆非國內之所能辦也。

translations.literal: If the labor and expense are like this, it is scarcely something the state can undertake.
translations.idiomatic: At such cost, the realm simply cannot afford it.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇下錮三泉，土未干而發毀。

translations.literal: The First Emperor of Qin sank down to seal three springs; before the earth was dry it was opened and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang buried himself beneath sealed springs, yet his tomb was looted before the soil had even dried.

sentences.zh: 自古無不亡之國、不掘之墓，故聖王之儉葬，乃深遠之慮也。

translations.literal: From antiquity there has been no state that did not perish and no tomb that was not dug up; therefore the sage kings' frugal burial was far-reaching deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: No kingdom endures forever, and no tomb escapes plunder. That is why the sage kings buried their dead modestly—it was foresight for the ages.

sentences.zh: 陛下奈何於中興之日，而踵亡國之事乎！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty, why on the day of restoration follow the deeds of a perished state!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, why on the day of dynastic revival would you repeat the blunders that destroyed a kingdom!"

sentences.zh: 曜下詔曰：「二侍中懇懇有古人之風，可謂社稷之臣矣。

translations.literal: Yao issued an edict, saying: "The two Attendants-in-Ordinary earnestly have the air of the ancients—they can be called ministers of the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yao then issued an edict: "These two attendants-in-ordinary speak with the earnest spirit of the ancients. They are true pillars of the state.

sentences.zh: 其悉罷宮室諸役，壽陵制度，一遵霸陵之法。

translations.literal: Let them fully halt all palace and construction labors; the Shou Mausoleum's specifications shall entirely follow the method of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Halt all palace construction at once, and let the Shou Mausoleum be built according to Baling's modest standard alone.

sentences.zh: 封豫安昌子，苞平輿子，並領諫議大夫；

translations.literal: Yu was enfeoffed as Viscount of Anchang, Bao as Viscount of Pingyu, both also holding the post of Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee;
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Qiao Yu as Viscount of Anchang and He Bao as Viscount of Pingyu, and appointed both as Remonstrance and Discussion Grandees;

sentences.zh: 仍佈告天下，使知區區之朝，欲聞其過也。」

translations.literal: Moreover a proclamation was issued to all under Heaven, to let them know this humble court desires to hear its faults."
translations.idiomatic: He further proclaimed throughout the realm that this small court wished to hear of its own failings."

sentences.zh: 又省酆水囿以與貧民。

translations.literal: He also reduced the Feng water park and gave it to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: He also reclaimed the Feng water royal park and distributed the land to impoverished commoners.

sentences.zh: 祖逖將韓潛與後趙將桃豹分據陳川故城，豹居西台，潛居東台，豹由南門，潛由東門，出入相守四旬，逖以布囊盛土如米狀，使千餘人運上台，又使數人擔米，息於道。

translations.literal: Zu Ti sent General Han Qian and the Later Zhao general Tao Bao to separately hold the old city of Chenchuan; Bao was at the west platform, Qian at the east platform; Bao used the south gate, Qian the east gate; for forty days they went in and out, keeping watch on each other. Zu Ti had cloth sacks filled with earth shaped like rice, had over a thousand men carry them up to the platform, and also had several men carry rice and rest on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti posted Han Qian and the Later Zhao general Tao Bao in separate quarters of the old Chenchuan walled city—Bao on the west tower, Qian on the east. Each used his own gate, south and east respectively, and for forty days they kept up a wary standoff. Zu Ti then had soldiers fill cloth sacks with earth shaped like grain sacks, and sent over a thousand men hauling them up to Qian's tower. He also sent a few men carrying real rice to pause and rest along the road.

sentences.zh: 豹兵逐之，棄擔而走。

translations.literal: Bao's soldiers pursued them; they dropped their carrying-poles and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's troops gave chase, but the carriers abandoned their loads and ran.

sentences.zh: 豹兵久饑，得米，以為逖士眾豐飽，益懼。

translations.literal: Bao's soldiers, long hungry, obtained the rice and thought Zu's troops and masses were abundantly fed; they grew more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's men, starving after a long siege, saw the grain and concluded that Zu Ti's forces were well provisioned. Their fear only grew.

sentences.zh: 後趙將劉夜堂以驢千頭運糧饋豹，逖使韓潛及別將馮鐵邀擊於汴水，盡獲之。

translations.literal: The Later Zhao general Liu Yetang used a thousand donkeys to transport grain to supply Bao; Zu sent Han Qian and the separate commander Feng Tie to intercept at the Bian River and captured it all.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Zhao general Liu Yetang tried to resupply Bao with a thousand donkey-loads of grain, Zu Ti sent Han Qian and Feng Tie to ambush the convoy at the Bian River and seized everything.

sentences.zh: 豹宵遁，屯東燕城，逖使潛進屯封丘以逼之。

translations.literal: Bao fled by night, encamped at Dongyan city; Zu sent Qian forward to encamp at Fengqiu to press him.
translations.idiomatic: Bao slipped away under cover of night and regrouped at Dongyan. Zu Ti then advanced Han Qian to Fengqiu to tighten the pressure.

sentences.zh: 馮鐵據二台，逖鎮雍丘，數遣兵邀擊後趙兵，後趙鎮戍歸逖者甚多，境土漸蹙。

translations.literal: Feng Tie held the two platforms; Zu garrisoned Yongqiu, repeatedly sent troops to intercept Later Zhao soldiers; many Later Zhao frontier garrisons returned to Zu, and the territory gradually narrowed.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Tie held both towers while Zu Ti made Yongqiu his headquarters. He sent raiding parties against Later Zhao columns again and again, and so many frontier garrisons defected to him that Zhao's foothold in the region steadily shrank.

sentences.zh: 先是，趙固、上官巳、李矩、郭默，互相攻擊，逖馳使和解之，示以禍福，遂皆受逖節度。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhao Gu, Shangguan Si, Li Ju, and Guo Mo had attacked one another; Zu sent envoys in haste to reconcile them, showing fortune and misfortune, and they all then accepted Zu's command.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Zhao Gu, Shangguan Si, Li Ju, and Guo Mo had been fighting among themselves. Zu Ti dispatched envoys to mediate, warning them of the consequences, and all four submitted to his authority.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，詔加逖鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: an edict added Zu as General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, the court promoted Zu Ti to General Who Guards the West.

sentences.zh: 逖在軍，與將士同甘苦，約己務施，勸課農桑，撫納新附，雖疏賤者皆結以恩禮。

translations.literal: When Zu was in the army, he shared weal and woe with officers and soldiers, restrained himself and devoted himself to generosity, encouraged farming and sericulture, comforted and received the newly submitted; even the remote and lowly he bound with grace and courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In camp Zu Ti lived as his men lived, sharing hardship and comfort alike. He kept himself austere while treating others generously, promoted agriculture, and welcomed new adherents with care. Even the humble and insignificant he won over with kindness and respect.

sentences.zh: 河上諸塢，先有任子在後趙者，皆聽兩屬，時遣遊軍偽抄之，明其未附。

translations.literal: The various fortified stockades along the river that had had sons serving in Later Zhao were all permitted dual allegiance; from time to time mobile detachments were sent to feign raids on them, to show they had not yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Stockades along the Yellow River whose sons still served in Later Zhao were allowed to straddle both sides. Zu Ti periodically sent raiding parties to strike them in feigned attacks, signaling to Later Zhao that they remained uncommitted.

sentences.zh: 塢主皆感恩，後趙有異謀，輒密以告，由是多所克獲，自河以南，多叛後趙歸於晉。

translations.literal: The stockade masters all were grateful; whenever Later Zhao had suspicious plots they would secretly inform him, and thereby many captures were made; from south of the river, many rebelled from Later Zhao and returned to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for this protection, the stockade chiefs often tipped him off when Later Zhao plotted against him. Zu Ti won many victories as a result, and south of the Yellow River, large numbers defected from Later Zhao to Jin.

sentences.zh: 逖練兵積穀，為取河北之計。

translations.literal: Zu drilled troops and amassed grain, planning to take Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti trained his army and stockpiled grain, preparing to drive into Hebei.

sentences.zh: 後趙王勒患之，乃下幽州為逖修祖、父墓，置守塚二家，因與逖書，求通使及互市。

translations.literal: The Later Zhao king Le was troubled by this; he therefore sent down to Youzhou to repair the tombs of Zu's grandfather and father, established two households to guard the graves, and thereby wrote to Zu, seeking exchange of envoys and mutual markets.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed by these gains, Later Zhao's King Le had Zu's ancestral tombs in Youzhou restored and two grave-keeping households appointed. Then he wrote to Zu Ti proposing diplomatic contact and cross-border trade.

sentences.zh: 逖不報書，而聽其互市，收利十倍。

translations.literal: Zu did not reply to the letter, but permitted the mutual market and reaped tenfold profit.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti ignored the letter but allowed the border markets to open, reaping tenfold profits from the trade.

sentences.zh: 逖牙門童建殺新蔡內史周密，降於後趙，勒斬之，送首於逖，曰：「叛臣逃吏，吾之深仇，將軍之惡，猶吾惡也。」

translations.literal: Zu's gate officer Tong Jian killed the Xincai Inspector Zhou Mi and surrendered to Later Zhao; Le executed him and sent the head to Zu, saying: "Rebellious ministers and fugitive officials are my deep enemies; what the general hates is like what I hate."
translations.idiomatic: Tong Jian, Zu Ti's gate officer, murdered Xincai's inspector Zhou Mi and defected to Later Zhao. Shi Le had him executed and sent his head to Zu Ti with a message: "Traitors and deserters are my sworn enemies, and I know they are yours as well."

sentences.zh: 逖深德之，自是後趙人叛歸逖者，逖皆不納，禁諸將不使侵暴後趙之民，邊境之間，稍得休息。

translations.literal: Zu was deeply grateful; from then on, when Later Zhao people rebelled and returned to Zu, Zu would not accept them, forbade his generals from letting them invade and brutalize Later Zhao's people, and between the borders there gradually came rest.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti was deeply moved. From then on he refused to accept defectors from Later Zhao, ordered his commanders not to harass Zhao civilians, and for a time the frontier grew quiet.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛未，梁州刺史周訪卒。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on the day xinwei, Liangzhou Inspector Zhou Fang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the xinwei day, Zhou Fang, Inspector of Liangzhou, died.

sentences.zh: 訪善於撫納士眾，皆為致死。

translations.literal: Fang was skilled at comforting and receiving officers and the masses; all would die for him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had a gift for winning over his troops, and they would fight to the death for him.

sentences.zh: 知王敦有不臣之心，私常切齒。

translations.literal: Knowing Wang Dun harbored disloyal intent, he privately often gnashed his teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Wang Dun's rebellious ambitions, he privately seethed with hatred.

sentences.zh: 敦由是終訪之世，未敢為逆。

translations.literal: Dun therefore through Fang's lifetime did not dare act rebelliously.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason Wang Dun never dared to rebel while Fang was alive.

sentences.zh: 敦遣從事中郎郭舒監襄陽軍，帝以湘州刺史甘卓為梁州刺史，督沔北諸軍事，鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: Dun sent Attendant of the Masters of Writing Guo Shu to supervise Xiangyang's army; the Emperor made Xiang Inspector Gan Zhuo Liangzhou Inspector, supervising all military affairs north of the Mian, garrisoning Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun dispatched Guo Shu, an attendant in the Masters of Writing, to oversee the Xiangyang garrison. The emperor replaced him as Inspector of Liangzhou with Gan Zhuo, governor of Xiangzhou, who took command of all forces north of the Mian and established headquarters at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 舒既還，帝征為右丞；

translations.literal: When Shu had returned, the Emperor summoned him as Right Vice Director;
translations.idiomatic: After Guo Shu returned, the emperor summoned him to serve as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: 敦留不遣。

translations.literal: Dun detained him and would not send him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun kept him and refused to let him go.

sentences.zh: 後趙王勒遣中山公虎帥步騎四萬擊徐龕，龕送妻子為質，乞降，勒許之。

translations.literal: The Later Zhao king Le sent the Duke of Zhongshan Hu leading forty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Xu Kan; Kan sent wife and children as hostages, begged to surrender, and Le consented.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao's King Le sent Shi Hu, Duke of Zhongshan, against Xu Kan at the head of forty thousand foot and horse. Kan sent his wife and children as hostages, sued for peace, and Le accepted his surrender.

sentences.zh: 蔡豹屯卞城，石虎將擊之，豹退守下邳，為徐龕所敗。

translations.literal: Cai Bao encamped at Biancheng; Shi Hu was about to attack him; Bao retreated to guard Xiapi and was defeated by Xu Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Bao held Biancheng until Shi Hu moved against him. Bao fell back to Xiapi, where Xu Kan routed him.

sentences.zh: 虎引兵城封丘而旋，徙士族三百家置襄國崇仁裡，置公族大夫以領之。

translations.literal: Hu led his troops to walled Fengqiu and returned, relocated three hundred clans of scholar-gentry and settled them in Chongren Lane in Xiangguo, and appointed a Grandee of the Public Clans to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu fortified Fengqiu and withdrew, resettling three hundred gentry families in Chongren Lane of Xiangguo and appointing a grandee to govern them.

sentences.zh: 後趙王勒用法甚嚴，諱「胡」尤峻。

translations.literal: The Later Zhao king Le was extremely strict in applying law, and tabooed the word "Hu" especially severely.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao's King Le enforced the law with brutal rigor, above all forbidding any use of the word hu—the term for barbarian.

sentences.zh: 宮殿既成，初有門戶之禁。

translations.literal: Once the palaces were completed, there were at first gate and portal prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace complex was finished, strict rules barred unauthorized entry through the gates.

sentences.zh: 有醉胡乘馬，突入止車門。

translations.literal: A drunk Hu rode a horse and burst through entering the Chariot-Halting Gate.
translations.idiomatic: One night a drunken tribesman on horseback crashed through the Chariot-Halting Gate.

sentences.zh: 勒大怒，責宮門小執法馮翥。

translations.literal: Le was greatly angry and reproached the minor gate law-enforcer Feng Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le flew into a rage and blamed Feng Xu, the minor gate officer on duty.

sentences.zh: 翥惶懼忘諱，對曰：「向有醉胡，乘馬馳入，甚呵御之，而不可與語。」

translations.literal: Xu, fearful and forgetful of the taboo, replied: "Just now there was a drunk Hu who rode a horse charging in; I greatly shouted at and drove him, yet could not speak with him."
translations.idiomatic: "There was a drunk barbarian," Feng Xu stammered in panic, forgetting the forbidden word himself, "who came galloping in on a horse. I shouted at him as loudly as I could, but he would not listen to reason."

sentences.zh: 勒笑曰：「胡人正自難與言。」

translations.literal: Le laughed and said: "Hu people are indeed hard to speak with."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le laughed and said, "Barbarians truly are impossible to reason with."

sentences.zh: 怒而不罪。

translations.literal: Angry yet did not punish.
translations.idiomatic: He was still angry, but he did not punish Feng Xu.

sentences.zh: 勒使張賓領選，初定五品，後更定九品。

translations.literal: Le had Zhang Bin lead selection; at first five grades were fixed, later nine grades were revised.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le put Zhang Bin in charge of recruitment, first establishing a five-rank system and later revising it to nine ranks.

sentences.zh: 命公卿及州郡歲舉秀才、至孝、廉清、賢良、直言、武勇之士各一人。

translations.literal: He ordered the public ministers and each province and commandery annually to recommend one each of outstanding talent, utmost filial piety, clean integrity, worthy goodness, forthright speech, and martial valor.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered ministers, provincial governors, and commandery officials to recommend one man each year from among candidates for literary excellence, filial devotion, clean integrity, moral worth, blunt honesty, and military valor.

sentences.zh: 西平公張茂立兄子駿為世子。

translations.literal: The Duke of Xiping Zhang Mao established his elder brother's son Jun as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao, Duke of Xiping, named his elder brother's son Zhang Jun as his heir.

sentences.zh: 蔡豹既敗，將詣建康歸罪，北中郎將王舒止之。

translations.literal: After Cai Bao had been defeated, he was about to go to Jiankang to acknowledge guilt; the North Commander-in-Chief Wang Shu stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat, Cai Bao prepared to go to Jiankang and surrender himself to judgment. Wang Shu, the North Commander-in-Chief, stopped him.

sentences.zh: 帝聞豹退，遣使收之。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard Bao had retreated and sent envoys to apprehend him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned that Bao had withdrawn, he dispatched officers to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 舒夜以兵圍豹，豹以為它寇，帥麾下擊之；

translations.literal: Shu by night surrounded Bao with troops; Bao thought it was another enemy and led his subordinates to attack them;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu encircled Bao by night with troops. Bao assumed another enemy had struck and led his men to counterattack;

sentences.zh: 聞有詔，乃止。

translations.literal: On hearing there was an imperial edict, he then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Only when he learned that an imperial order had arrived did he halt.

sentences.zh: 舒執豹送建康，冬，十月，丙辰，斬之。

translations.literal: Shu seized Bao and sent him to Jiankang; winter, tenth month, on the day bingchen, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu seized Bao and sent him to Jiankang. In the tenth month of winter, on the bingchen day, Cai Bao was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 王敦殺武陵內史向碩。

translations.literal: Wang Dun killed Wuling Interior Minister Xiang Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun had Xiang Shuo, interior minister of Wuling, put to death.

sentences.zh: 帝之始鎮江東也，敦與從弟導同心翼戴，帝亦推心任之，敦總征討，導專機政，群從子弟布列顯要，時人為之語曰：「王與馬，共天下。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor first garrisoned the lands east of the Yangtze, Dun and his cousin Dao together supported and bore him aloft; the Emperor also placed his heart in them and entrusted them; Dun controlled campaigns and punishments, Dao monopolized vital policy; their clansmen and nephews filled prominent posts. People of the time made a saying of it: "The Wangs and the Mas share the realm."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first established his court east of the Yangtze, Wang Dun and his cousin Wang Dao stood by him as loyal pillars, and he in turn entrusted them wholeheartedly. Dun held military command, while Dao ran the civil government; their kinsmen filled every important post. People said at the time, "The Wangs and the Mas share the empire."

sentences.zh: 後敦自恃有功，且宗族強盛，稍益驕恣，帝畏而惡之。

translations.literal: Later Dun, relying on his merits and moreover on his clan's strength, gradually grew more arrogant and willful; the Emperor feared and despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Dun, taking credit for his service and bolstered by his powerful clan, grew steadily more arrogant. The emperor came to fear and loathe him.

sentences.zh: 乃引劉隗、刁協等以為腹心，稍抑損王氏之權，導亦漸見疏外。

translations.literal: He therefore drew in Liu Kai, Diao Xie, and others as his trusted inner circle, gradually reduced the Wang clan's power, and Dao also gradually came to be seen as estranged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Liu Kai, Diao Xie, and others as his inner circle, and little by little he curtailed Wang power. Wang Dao, too, was gradually pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 中書郎孔愉陳導忠賢，有佐命之勳，宜加委任；

translations.literal: Zhongshu Lang Kong Yu stated that Dao was loyal and worthy, had merit in assisting the mandate, and should receive increased appointment;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu Lang Kong Yu argued that Wang Dao was loyal and worthy, had helped establish the dynasty, and deserved greater trust;

sentences.zh: 帝出愉為司徒左長史。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Yu out as Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded by posting Kong Yu away as Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 導能任真推分，澹如也，有識皆稱其善處興廢。

translations.literal: Dao was able to be genuine and yield his share, calm and composed; those with insight all praised his fine handling of rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao accepted his diminished role with quiet grace, and observers admired how well he weathered fortune's turns.

sentences.zh: 而敦益懷不平，遂構嫌隙。

translations.literal: But Dun grew all the more resentful and thus built up mutual suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun, meanwhile, grew ever more resentful, and bad blood between them hardened.

sentences.zh: 初，敦辟吳興沈充為參軍，充薦同郡錢鳳於敦，敦以為鎧曹參軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dun had recruited Shen Chong of Wuxing as an aide; Chong recommended his fellow countryman Qian Feng to Dun, and Dun made him Aide in the Armor Section.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Wang Dun had taken Shen Chong of Wuxing as a staff officer. Chong recommended his fellow townsman Qian Feng, whom Dun appointed aide in the armor section.

sentences.zh: 二人皆巧諂凶狡，知敦有異志，陰贊成之，為之畫策。

translations.literal: Both men were crafty in flattery, fierce and cunning; knowing Dun had divergent intent, they secretly helped bring it about and devised plans for him.
translations.idiomatic: Both were sycophantic and ruthless. Sensing Dun's rebellious designs, they secretly encouraged them and plotted on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 敦寵信之，勢傾內外。

translations.literal: Dun favored and trusted them; their power overbore inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun lavished trust on them, and their influence eclipsed everyone at court and in the field.

sentences.zh: 敦上疏為導訟屈，辭語怨望。

translations.literal: Dun submitted a memorial pleading Dao's wrong, with language full of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun petitioned the throne on Wang Dao's behalf, his language bristling with grievance.

sentences.zh: 導封以還敦，敦復遣奏之。

translations.literal: Dao sealed it and returned it to Dun; Dun again sent it in as a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao sealed the petition and sent it back unread; Dun simply submitted it again.

sentences.zh: 左將軍譙王承，忠厚有志行，帝親信之。

translations.literal: Left General the Prince of Qiao Cheng was loyal and generous with purpose and conduct; the Emperor personally trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Left General Sima Cheng, Prince of Qiao, was loyal, principled, and trusted personally by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 夜，召承，以敦疏示之，曰：「王敦以頃年之功，位任足矣；

translations.literal: At night he summoned Cheng, showed him Dun's memorial, and said: "Wang Dun, with his merits of recent years, position and responsibility are enough;
translations.idiomatic: One night the emperor summoned Cheng, showed him Wang Dun's memorial, and said, "Given what Wang Dun has accomplished these past years, his rank and honors should be enough;

sentences.zh: 而所求不已，言至於此，將若之何？」

translations.literal: yet his demands never cease—his words have come to this; what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: yet his demands never stop. He has gone this far—what are we to do?"

sentences.zh: 承曰：「陛下不早裁之，以至今日，敦必為患。」

translations.literal: Cheng said: "Your Majesty did not cut this off early, until today—Dun will surely become a calamity.'
translations.idiomatic: Cheng replied, "Your Majesty failed to check him in time, and now he is certain to become a grave threat.'

sentences.zh: 劉隗為帝謀，出心腹以鎮方面。

translations.literal: Liu Kai plotted for the Emperor, sending trusted inner men to garrison the regions.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kai advised the emperor to post trusted lieutenants to key regional commands.

sentences.zh: 會敦表以宣城內史沈充代甘卓為湘州刺史，帝謂承曰：「王敦奸逆已著，朕為惠皇，其勢不遠。

translations.literal: When Dun submitted a memorial proposing Xuancheng Interior Minister Shen Chong replace Gan Zhuo as Xiang Inspector, the Emperor said to Cheng: "Wang Dun's treachery and rebellion are already evident; I shall be like Emperor Hui—his momentum is not far.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun petitioned to replace Gan Zhuo as governor of Xiangzhou with Shen Chong, the emperor told Cheng, "Wang Dun's treason is plain. Unless we act, I will end like Emperor Hui—the doom is not far off.

sentences.zh: 湘州據上流之勢，控三州之會，欲以叔父居之，何如？」

translations.literal: Xiang province holds the advantage of the upper reaches, controls the junction of three provinces—I wish to have my uncle reside there; what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzhou commands the upper Yangtze and the meeting point of three provinces. I want to send my uncle to govern it—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 承曰：「臣奉承詔命，惟力是視，何敢有辭！

translations.literal: Cheng said: "Your servant receives the imperial command—only strength is to be looked to; how dare there be words!
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "I accept your command and will do all I can. I would not refuse it!

sentences.zh: 然湘州經蜀寇之餘，民物凋弊，若得之部，比及三年，乃可即戎；

translations.literal: Yet Xiang province, after the ravages of Shu bandits, has people and goods in decline; if one obtains that province, by three years one may take up arms;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xiangzhou has been devastated by the Shu raids. Even if my uncle takes office there, it will be three years before the province is ready for war;

sentences.zh: 苟未及此，雖復灰身，亦無益也。」

translations.literal: if it has not reached this, even again reducing the body to ashes would be of no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: and before then, even if he gave his life, it would do no good."

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔曰：「晉室開基，方鎮之任，親賢並用，其以譙王承為湘州刺史。」

translations.literal: Twelfth month, an edict said: "The Jin house established its foundation; in the charge of frontier commands, kin and worthies were used together. Let the Prince of Qiao Cheng be made Xiang Inspector."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month an edict declared, "Since the founding of Jin, frontier commands have been entrusted to both royal kin and capable men alike. Sima Cheng, Prince of Qiao, is appointed Inspector of Xiangzhou."

sentences.zh: 長沙鄧騫聞之，歎曰：「湘州之禍，其在斯乎！」

translations.literal: Changsha's Deng Qian, hearing this, sighed and said: "The calamity of Xiang province—surely it lies here!"
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Qian of Changsha heard the news, he sighed, "The disaster destined for Xiangzhou begins here!"

sentences.zh: 承行至武昌，敦與之宴，謂承曰：「大王雅素佳士，恐非將帥才也。」

translations.literal: Cheng traveled to Wuchang; Dun feasted with him and said to Cheng: "Great King, elegantly and always a fine gentleman—I fear you are not talent for generalship."
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng reached Wuchang, Wang Dun entertained him and said, "Your Highness is a refined gentleman, but I doubt you have the makings of a military commander."

sentences.zh: 承曰：「公未見知耳，鉛刀豈無一割之用！」

translations.literal: Cheng said: "You have not yet known me—a lead knife—can it not have one cut's use!"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng replied, "You simply do not know me yet. Even a blunt lead knife can still cut once!"

sentences.zh: 敦謂錢鳳曰：「彼不知懼而學壯語，足知其不武，無能為也。」

translations.literal: Dun said to Qian Feng: "He does not know fear yet learns bold words—enough to know he is not martial; he cannot act."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun told Qian Feng, "He shows no fear and talks big—that tells me he lacks real courage. He will be no trouble."

sentences.zh: 乃聽之鎮。

translations.literal: He therefore permitted him to take up the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: So Wang Dun let him proceed to his post.

sentences.zh: 時湘土荒殘，公私困弊，承躬自儉約，傾心綏撫，甚有能名。

translations.literal: At that time the Xiang region was desolate and ruined, public and private exhausted and impoverished; Cheng personally was frugal and restrained, devoting his heart to pacification and comfort, and had great reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzhou was then a wasteland, the treasury and people alike impoverished. Cheng lived modestly, devoted himself wholly to relief and governance, and quickly won a strong reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 高句麗寇遼東，慕容仁與戰，大破之，自是不敢犯仁境。

translations.literal: Koguryo raided Liaodong; Murong Ren fought them and greatly defeated them; from then on they did not dare violate Ren's territory.
translations.idiomatic: When Koguryo invaded Liaodong, Murong Ren met them in battle and routed them soundly. They never again dared cross into his territory.

sentences.zh: 中宗元皇帝中太興四年（

translations.literal: Within the reign of Emperor Yuan of the Middle Era, the fourth year of Taixing (
translations.idiomatic: Within the reign of Emperor Yuan, fourth year of the Taixing era (

sentences.zh: 辛巳，公元三二一年）

translations.literal: xin Year of the Snake, AD 321)
translations.idiomatic: xin Year of the Snake, 321 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，徐龕復請降。

translations.literal: Spring, second month: Xu Kan again requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring, Xu Kan once again sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 張茂築靈鈞台，基高九仞。

translations.literal: Zhang Mao built the Lingjun Terrace, its foundation nine ren high.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao built the Lingjun Terrace on a foundation nine ren high.

sentences.zh: 武陵閻曾夜叩府門呼曰：「武公遣我來，言『何故勞民築台！』」

translations.literal: Wuling's Yan Zeng by night knocked on the prefectural gate calling out: "Duke Wu sent me, saying 'Why do you exhaust the people to build a terrace!
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zeng of Wuling came pounding on the governor's gate at night, shouting, "Duke Wu sent me to ask, 'Why are you exhausting the people to build this terrace!

sentences.zh: 有司以為妖，請殺之。

translations.literal: The officials regarded it as portentous and requested to kill him.'
translations.idiomatic: The officials called it sorcery and asked that Yan Zeng be executed.'

sentences.zh: 茂曰：「吾信勞民。

translations.literal: Mao said: "I believe I exhaust the people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao said, "He is right that I have exhausted the people.

sentences.zh: 曾稱先君之命以規我，何謂妖呼！」

translations.literal: Zeng invoked our late lord's command to admonish me—why call it portentous shouting!"
translations.idiomatic: He spoke in my father's name to warn me—how can that be called sorcery!"

sentences.zh: 乃為之罷役。

translations.literal: He therefore for this halted the labor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao then stopped the work.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸亥，日中有黑子。

translations.literal: Third month, on the day guihai, there was a black spot in the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the guihai day, a black spot appeared on the sun.

sentences.zh: 著作佐郎河東郭璞以帝用刑過差，上疏，以為：「陰陽錯繆，皆繁刑所致。

translations.literal: Associate Editor of the Historiography Office Guo Pu of Hedong, because the Emperor's use of punishments exceeded proper measure, submitted a memorial, holding: "Yin and yang are disordered and confused—all caused by excessive punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu of Hedong, associate editor in the historiography office, submitted a memorial arguing that the emperor's punishments had grown excessive. He wrote, "When yin and yang fall out of balance, it is because punishments have grown too severe.

sentences.zh: 赦不欲數，然子產知鑄刑書非政之善，不得不作者，須以救弊故也。

translations.literal: Amnesties one does not wish to issue frequently; yet Zichan knew that casting the penal code in bronze was not a good policy, yet what could not be omitted in writing had to be done, because one must use it to remedy abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesties should not be issued too often, yet Zichan knew that casting penal statutes in bronze was no mark of good government—still, when written law becomes unavoidable, it is because the times demand a remedy for abuse.

sentences.zh: 今之宜赦，理亦如之。」

translations.literal: The appropriateness of amnesty today follows the same principle.'
translations.idiomatic: The case for an amnesty now rests on the same reasoning.'

sentences.zh: 後趙中山公虎攻幽州刺史段匹磾於厭次，孔萇攻其統內諸城，悉拔之。

translations.literal: Later Zhao's Duke of Zhongshan Hu attacked Youzhou Inspector Duan Pidi at Yanci; Kong Chang attacked the various cities within his domain and pulled them all out.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu, Duke of Zhongshan, besieged Duan Pidi, Inspector of Youzhou, at Yanci, while Kong Chang overran and captured every city in Pidi's domain.

sentences.zh: 段文鴦言於匹磾曰：「我以勇聞，故為民所倚望。

translations.literal: Duan Wenyang said to Pidi: "I am known for courage, and therefore am relied on and looked to by the people.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Wenyang told Pidi, "My reputation rests on courage—that is why the people look to me.

sentences.zh: 今視民被掠而不救，是怯也。

translations.literal: Now to see the people plundered yet not rescue them—this is cowardice.
translations.idiomatic: If I watch them being pillaged and do nothing, I will have shown myself a coward.

sentences.zh: 民失所望，誰復為我致死！」

translations.literal: The people will lose hope—who again will die for me!
translations.idiomatic: Once the people lose faith in me, who will ever die in my cause again?

sentences.zh: 遂帥壯士數十騎出戰，殺後趙兵甚眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led several dozen mounted stalwarts out to battle and killed very many Later Zhao soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He then rode out with several dozen picked warriors and cut down a great many Later Zhao troops.

sentences.zh: 馬乏，伏不能起。

translations.literal: His horse was exhausted; he collapsed prone and could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: His horse gave out, and he fell to the ground and could not get up.

sentences.zh: 虎呼之曰：「兄與我俱夷狄，久欲與兄同為一家。

translations.literal: Hu called out to him, saying: 'You and I are both barbarians of the Yi and Di; for long I have wished to be one family with you, Elder Brother.
translations.idiomatic: Hu shouted to him, 'Brother, we are both barbarians by birth. I have long wanted us to stand as one family.

sentences.zh: 今天不違願，於此得相見，何為復戰！

translations.literal: Today my wish is not denied; here I obtain to meet you—why still fight!
translations.idiomatic: Today that wish is fulfilled—we meet face to face at last. Why fight on!

sentences.zh: 請釋仗。」

translations.literal: I beg you lay down your weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Please drop your arms.

sentences.zh: 文鴦罵曰：「汝為寇賊，當死日久，吾兄不用吾策，故令汝得至此。

translations.literal: Wenyang cursed, saying: 'You are a bandit-robber—long since you should have died. My elder brother did not use my plan, and so let you reach this point.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyang cursed back, 'You are a brigand who should have died long ago. My brother refused my counsel—that is how you got this far.

sentences.zh: 我寧斗死，不為汝屈！」

translations.literal: I would rather die fighting than submit to you!
translations.idiomatic: I will die fighting before I ever bow to you!

sentences.zh: 遂下馬苦戰，槊折，執刀戰不已，自辰至申。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dismounted and fought bitterly; his spear broke, he took up a blade and fought without cease, from the hour chen to the hour shen.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted and fought on foot. When his spear snapped he drew a sword and kept fighting—from mid-morning until late afternoon.

sentences.zh: 後趙兵四面解馬羅披自鄣，前執文鴦；

translations.literal: From all four sides Later Zhao soldiers unfastened horses and linked horse-trappings and shields into walls, and from the front seized Wenyang;
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao troops closed in from every side, dismounting to lock shields and horses into a living barricade, then seized Wenyang from the front;

sentences.zh: 文鴦力竭被執，城內奪氣。

translations.literal: Wenyang, strength exhausted, was seized; within the city morale collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyang's strength gave out and he was captured, and the city's defenders lost heart.

sentences.zh: 匹磾欲單騎歸朝，邵續之弟樂安內史洎勒兵不聽。

translations.literal: Pidi wished to return to court alone on horseback; Ji, younger brother of Shao Xu and Interior Administrator of Lean, drew up troops and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Pidi wanted to ride alone back to the imperial court, but Ji—Shao Xu's younger brother and Interior Administrator of Lean—mobilized his troops and refused to let him go.

sentences.zh: 洎復欲執台使王英送於虎，匹磾正色責之曰：「卿不能遵兄之志，逼吾不得歸朝，亦已甚矣！

translations.literal: Ji again wished to seize the court envoy Wang Ying and deliver him to Hu. Pidi, with stern countenance, rebuked him, saying: 'You cannot follow your elder brother's intent, forcing me not to return to court—that is already going too far!
translations.idiomatic: Ji then planned to seize the imperial envoy Wang Ying and hand him over to Hu. Pidi confronted him sternly: 'You refuse to honor your brother's will and already block my return to court—that is outrage enough!

sentences.zh: 復欲執天子使者？

translations.literal: And now you would seize the Son of Heaven's envoy?
translations.idiomatic: Would you now seize an envoy of the emperor?

sentences.zh: 我雖夷狄，所未聞也！」

translations.literal: Though I am a barbarian of the Yi and Di, this I have never heard of!
translations.idiomatic: I am a barbarian myself, yet even I have never heard of such a thing!

sentences.zh: 洎與兄子緝、竺等輿櫬出降。

translations.literal: Ji, together with his elder brother's sons Ji and Zhu and others, went out to surrender carrying coffins on carts.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, his nephew Ji, Zhu, and others went out carrying coffins on carts to surrender.

sentences.zh: 匹磾見虎曰：「我受晉恩，志在滅汝，不幸至此，不能為汝敬也。」

translations.literal: Pidi, meeting Hu, said: 'I received Jin grace; my intent was to destroy you. Unfortunate that I have come to this—I cannot show you respect.
translations.idiomatic: When Pidi met Hu he said, 'I owe the Jin dynasty a debt of gratitude. My purpose was to destroy you. It is my misfortune to stand here—I cannot show you obeisance.

sentences.zh: 後趙王勒及虎素與匹磾結為兄弟，虎即起拜之。

translations.literal: Later Zhao King Le and Hu had long been sworn brothers with Pidi; Hu immediately rose and bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le, King of Later Zhao, and Hu had long treated Pidi as a sworn brother, and Hu at once rose and paid him formal respect.

sentences.zh: 勒以匹磾為冠軍將軍，文鴦為左中郎將，散諸流民三萬餘戶，復其本業，置守宰以撫之。

translations.literal: Le appointing Pidi Champion General and Wenyang Left Commandant of the Palace Guard, dispersed the various displaced persons of more than thirty thousand households, restored their original occupations, and set overseers and magistrates to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Le made Pidi Champion General and Wenyang Left Commandant of the Palace Guard. More than thirty thousand refugee households were resettled to their former trades, with officials appointed to oversee and comfort them.

sentences.zh: 於是幽、冀、並三州皆入於後趙。

translations.literal: Thereupon You, Ji, and Bing—the three provinces—all entered into Later Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: With that, the three provinces of You, Ji, and Bing all fell under Later Zhao's control.

sentences.zh: 匹磾不為勒禮，常著朝服，持晉節；

translations.literal: Pidi did not perform obeisance to Le; he constantly wore court robes and held Jin credentials;
translations.idiomatic: Pidi refused to bow to Le, continuing to wear Jin court dress and carry the Jin imperial staff of office;

sentences.zh: 久之，與文鴦、邵續皆為後趙所殺。

translations.literal: After long time, he together with Wenyang and Shao Xu were all killed by Later Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In time, Pidi, Wenyang, and Shao Xu were all put to death by Later Zhao.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚申，詔免中州良民遭難為揚州諸郡僮客者，以備征役。

translations.literal: Fifth month, gengshen: an edict exempted Central Province good commoners who, having suffered calamity, had become retainers and clients in the various commanderies of Yangzhou, so as to prepare them for corvée and military service.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the gengshen day, an edict released Central Plains refugees who had been forced into bond service in Yangzhou's commanderies, drafting them for military levy instead.

sentences.zh: 尚書令刁協之謀也，由是眾益怨之。

translations.literal: This was the stratagem of Shangshu Ling Diao Xie; from this the multitude increasingly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: The plan came from Diao Xie, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and popular resentment toward him only deepened.

sentences.zh: 終南山崩。

translations.literal: Zhongnan Mountain collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Zhongnan collapsed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲戌，以尚書僕射戴淵為征西將軍、都督司、兗、豫、並、雍、冀六州諸軍事、司州刺史，鎮合肥；

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, jiaxu: Dai Yuan, Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made General Who Pacifies the West, Supervisor of Military Affairs for the six provinces Si, Yan, Yu, Bing, Yong, and Ji, and Inspector of Si, garrisoning Hefei;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the jiaxu day, Dai Yuan was appointed General Who Pacifies the West, commander of military affairs in Si, Yan, Yu, Bing, Yong, and Ji, and Inspector of Si, with headquarters at Hefei;

sentences.zh: 丹楊尹劉隗為鎮北將軍、都督青、徐、幽、平四州諸軍事、青州刺史，鎮淮陰。

translations.literal: Liu Kai, Prefect of Danyang, was made General Who Pacifies the North, Supervisor of Military Affairs for the four provinces Qing, Xu, You, and Ping, and Inspector of Qing, garrisoning Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kai, Prefect of Danyang, became General Who Pacifies the North, with command over Qing, Xu, You, and Ping, and Inspector of Qing, stationed at Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 皆假節領兵，名為討胡，實備王敦也。

translations.literal: Both were granted credential-bearers' staffs and commanded troops; nominally to campaign against the Hu, but in fact to guard against Wang Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Both received acting imperial authority and field commands officially to campaign against barbarian foes, but in truth to guard against Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 隗雖在外，而朝廷機事，進退士大夫，帝皆與之密謀。

translations.literal: Though Kai was outside the capital, the Court's critical affairs—the advancement and dismissal of gentry and officials—the Emperor all secretly plotted with him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Liu Kai was posted far from the capital, the emperor consulted him in secret on every crucial matter of state, including appointments and dismissals among the scholar-official class.

sentences.zh: 敦遺隗書曰：「頃承聖上顧眄足下，今大賊未滅，中原鼎沸，欲與足下及周生之徒戮力王室，共靜海內。

translations.literal: Dun sent Kai a letter, saying: 'Recently I have heard that His Sagely Majesty has favored you with his gaze. Now the great enemy is not yet destroyed, the Central Plains are boiling like a cauldron; I wish with you and men like Zhou Yan to exert our strength for the royal house and together pacify the realm within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun wrote to Liu Kai: 'I hear the emperor has lately favored you with his trust. The great enemy is not yet destroyed and the Central Plains are in turmoil. I hope to join you and men of Zhou Yan's stamp in throwing our strength behind the throne and pacifying the empire.

sentences.zh: 若其泰也，則帝祚於是乎隆；

translations.literal: If it goes well, then the imperial fortune will from this ascend;
translations.idiomatic: If we succeed, the dynasty will flourish;

sentences.zh: 若其否也，則天下永無望矣。」

translations.literal: If it goes ill, then the realm under Heaven will forever have no hope.
translations.idiomatic: if we fail, there will be no hope left for the realm.

sentences.zh: 隗答曰：「『魚相忘於江湖，人相忘於道術。』

translations.literal: Kai replied: ''Fish forget each other in rivers and lakes; men forget each other in the Way and its arts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kai replied, ''Let fish forget one another in rivers and lakes, and let men forget one another in their separate paths.

sentences.zh: 『竭股肱之力，效力以忠貞』，吾之志也。」

translations.literal: 'To exhaust the strength of arm and thigh and serve with loyalty and integrity'—this is my intent.'
translations.idiomatic: 'To give every ounce of one's strength in loyal service'—that is my purpose.'

sentences.zh: 敦得書，甚怒。

translations.literal: Dun received the letter and was very angry.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun read the reply, he flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以驃騎將軍王導為侍中、司空、假節、錄尚書、領中書監。

translations.literal: Renwu: Wang Dao, General of Agile Cavalry, was made Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, acting credential-bearer, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Concurrent Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day, Wang Dao was made Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, acting imperial commissioner, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Chief of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝以敦故，並疏忌導。

translations.literal: Because of Dun, the Emperor also kept Dao at a distance and was suspicious of him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Wang Dun, the emperor kept Wang Dao at arm's length and viewed him with suspicion.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞周嵩上疏，以為：「導忠素竭誠，輔成大業，不宜聽孤臣之言，惑疑似之說，放逐舊德，以佞伍賢，虧既往之恩，招將來之患。」

translations.literal: Imperial Censor Zhou Song memorialized, holding that: 'Dao has long been loyal and wholehearted, assisting to accomplish the great enterprise; one should not heed the words of an isolated minister, be confused by half-suspected talk, banish old merit, put sycophants in the company of the worthy, impair grace already shown, and invite calamity yet to come.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Song, Imperial Censor, submitted a memorial arguing that Wang Dao's loyalty was proven and that he had helped build the dynasty. 'Do not let a disloyal minister's whispering,' he wrote, 'or vague suspicions drive you to cast aside a proven servant, surround the worthy with flatterers, betray past kindness, and invite future disaster.

sentences.zh: 帝頗感寤，導由是得全。

translations.literal: The Emperor was somewhat moved to awareness; Dao thereby was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was partly persuaded, and Wang Dao was spared.

sentences.zh: 八月，常山崩。

translations.literal: Eighth month: Changshan Mountain collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Mount Chang collapsed.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史祖逖，以戴淵吳士，雖有才望，無弘致遠識；

translations.literal: Zu Ti, Inspector of Yu Province, considered Dai Yuan a man of Wu—though he had talent and prestige, he lacked broad far-reaching insight;
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti, Inspector of Yu Province, regarded Dai Yuan as a man of Wu: talented and respected, but without the grand vision needed for long-range planning;

sentences.zh: 且己翦荊棘、收河南地，而淵雍容，一旦來統之，意甚怏怏；

translations.literal: Moreover, he himself had cut thorns and brambles and recovered Henan territory, yet Yuan was at ease and unhurried—suddenly coming to command him—his mind was very displeased;
translations.idiomatic: He himself had cleared the north of enemies and recovered territory south of the Yellow River, only to have the leisurely Dai Yuan arrive and take command overnight. The affront rankled deeply;

sentences.zh: 又聞王敦與劉、刁構隙，將有內難，知大功不遂，感激發病；

translations.literal: Also he heard that Wang Dun and Liu and Diao had built enmity, that there would soon be internal trouble—knowing great achievement would not be accomplished, stirred to passion he fell ill;
translations.idiomatic: He also learned that Wang Dun was feuding with Liu Kai and Diao Xie and that civil strife was brewing. Seeing his larger mission doomed, he fell ill from grief and frustration;

sentences.zh: 九月，壬寅，卒於雍丘。

translations.literal: Ninth month, renyin: he died at Yongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the renyin day, he died at Yongqiu.

sentences.zh: 豫州士女若喪父母，譙、梁間皆為立祠。

translations.literal: The gentlemen and women of Yu Province were as if bereaved of parents; between Qiao and Liang all erected shrines for him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yu Province mourned him as they would their own parents, and shrines to his memory sprang up throughout the region between Qiao and Liang.

sentences.zh: 王敦久懷異志，聞逖卒，益無所憚。

translations.literal: Wang Dun for long had harbored divergent intent; hearing Ti had died, he was increasingly without anything to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun had long nursed rebellious designs, and Zu Ti's death removed the last check on his ambitions.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬午，以逖弟約為平西將軍、豫州刺史，領逖之眾。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, renwu: Ti's younger brother Yue was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yu Province, taking over Ti's forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the renwu day, Zu Ti's brother Zu Yue was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yu Province, inheriting his brother's army.

sentences.zh: 約無綏御之才，不為士卒所附。

translations.literal: Yue lacked talent to pacify and control; the soldiers did not attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue lacked his brother's gift for command, and the troops gave him little loyalty.

sentences.zh: 初，范陽李產避亂依逖，見約志趣異常，謂所親曰：「吾以北方鼎沸，故遠來就此，冀全宗族。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Chan of Fanyang, fleeing turmoil, had relied on Ti. Seeing Yue's ambition and intent were abnormal, he said to those close to him: 'Because the north was boiling like a cauldron, I came far to attach here, hoping to preserve my clan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Chan of Fanyang had taken refuge with Zu Ti during the chaos. When he saw Zu Yue's strange ambitions, he told his friends, 'I came south because the north was in flames, hoping to save my clan.

sentences.zh: 今觀約所為，有不可測之志。

translations.literal: Now observing Yue's conduct, there is an intent that cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Now I see where Zu Yue is heading, and it is a path no one can predict.

sentences.zh: 吾托名姻親，當早自為計，無事復陷身於不義也，爾曹不可以目前之利而忘久長之策。」

translations.literal: I borrow the name of marriage affinity—I ought early to make my own plans; there is no reason again to plunge myself into unrighteousness. You all must not because of present profit forget long-term strategy.
translations.idiomatic: We are connected by marriage, and I must look out for myself before it is too late. There is no point in being swept into something shameful again. Do not trade a lasting future for a moment's gain.

sentences.zh: 乃帥子弟十餘人間行歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led more than ten family members and younger relatives by secret paths back to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He then took more than a dozen kin and slipped away by back roads to their home country.

sentences.zh: 十一月，皇孫衍生。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: the imperial grandson Yan was born.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, the emperor's grandson Yan was born.

sentences.zh: 後趙王勒悉召武鄉耆舊詣襄國，與之共坐歡飲。

translations.literal: Later Zhao King Le fully summoned the elders and old associates of Wuxiang to Xiangguo, sat together with them drinking in merriment.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le summoned every elder statesman of his native Wuxiang to Xiangguo and shared seats and cups with them in celebration.

sentences.zh: 初，勒微時，與李陽鄰居，數爭漚麻池相毆，陽由是獨不敢來。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Le was obscure, he and Li Yang were neighbors; they repeatedly fought over the hemp-retting pool and battered each other—Yang for this reason alone dared not come.
translations.idiomatic: In Le's early days he and Li Yang had been neighbors and often brawled over access to the hemp-retting pool, which was why Yang alone stayed away.

sentences.zh: 勒曰：「陽，壯士也；

translations.literal: Le said: 'Yang is a stalwart;
translations.idiomatic: Le said, 'Li Yang is a brave man;

sentences.zh: 漚麻，布衣之恨；

translations.literal: hemp-retting—a commoner's grudge;
translations.idiomatic: A quarrel over soaking hemp is a peasant's grudge;

sentences.zh: 孤方兼容天下，豈仇匹夫乎！」

translations.literal: I am now broadly accommodating all under Heaven—how would I bear a grudge against a single common man!
translations.idiomatic: I intend to embrace the whole empire—why would I bear a grudge against one ordinary man!

sentences.zh: 遽召與飲，引陽臂曰：「孤往日厭卿老拳，卿亦飽孤毒手。」

translations.literal: He immediately summoned him to drink, pulled Yang's arm, and said: 'In days past I was weary of your old fists—you also have had your fill of my vicious hands.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yang brought in at once, took his arm, and said with a laugh, 'I used to dread your heavy fists—and you surely remember mine.

sentences.zh: 因拜參軍都尉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed Staff Adjutant Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Yang Staff Adjutant Commandant.

sentences.zh: 以武鄉比豐、沛，復之三世。

translations.literal: He compared Wuxiang to Feng and Pei, exempting it for three generations.
translations.idiomatic: He exempted Wuxiang from taxes for three generations, granting it privileges comparable to Liu Bang's home counties of Feng and Pei.

sentences.zh: 勒以民始復業，資儲未豐，於是重制禁釀，郊祀宗廟，皆用醴酒，行之數年，無復釀者。

translations.literal: Le, because the people were only beginning to restore their occupations and stores were not yet abundant, therefore strictly reinstituted prohibition of brewing; suburban sacrifices and ancestral temples all used sacrificial ale, and after practicing this for several years there were no longer any brewers.
translations.idiomatic: Because the people were just returning to their fields and grain reserves were still thin, Le banned private brewing entirely. State rituals alone could use ritual wine, and within a few years private distillation had virtually ceased.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以慕容廆為都督幽、平二州、東夷諸軍事、車騎將軍、平州牧，封遼東公，單于如故，遣謁者即授印綬，聽承製置官司守宰。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Murong Hui was made Supervisor of Military Affairs for You and Ping provinces and Eastern Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Governor of Ping Province, enfeoffed as Duke of Liaodong, chanyu as before; an usher was dispatched to confer seals and cords on the spot, permitted to accept and establish official bureaus, magistrates, and overseers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Murong Hui was confirmed as commander of You and Ping, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Governor of Ping, and Duke of Liaodong, retaining his title as chanyu. An imperial envoy invested him with seal and ribbon on the spot and authorized him to appoint his own officials and local administrators.

sentences.zh: 廆於是備置僚屬，以裴嶷、游邃為長史，裴開為司馬，韓壽為別駕，陽耽為軍諮祭酒，崔燾為主簿，黃泓、鄭林參軍事。

translations.literal: Hui thereupon fully set up staff and assistants, appointing Pei Yi and You Sui as Chief Clerks, Pei Kai as Major, Han Shou as Escort Commander, Yang Dan as Military Adviser Sacrificer, Cui Tao as Registrar, and Huang Hong and Zheng Lin as staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then assembled a full administrative staff: Pei Yi and You Sui as chief clerks, Pei Kai as Major, Han Shou as Escort Commander, Yang Dan as military adviser, Cui Tao as registrar, and Huang Hong and Zheng Lin as adjutants.

sentences.zh: 廆立子皝為世子。

translations.literal: Hui established his son Huang as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Hui named his son Huang heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 作東橫，以平原劉贊為祭酒，使皝與諸生同受業，廆得暇，亦親臨聽之。

translations.literal: He built the Eastern Transverse Hall, appointing Liu Zan of Pingyuan as Libationer, causing Huang together with the various students to receive instruction alike; when Hui had leisure, he also personally came to listen.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Eastern Hall of Learning, with Liu Zan of Pingyuan as its rector, and had Huang study alongside the other pupils. When his duties allowed, Hui himself attended to listen.

sentences.zh: 皝雄毅多權略，喜經術，國人稱之。

translations.literal: Huang was bold and resolute, rich in stratagems, fond of the classic arts—the people of the state praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was bold, resourceful, and devoted to the classics, and his countrymen spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 廆徙慕容翰鎮遼東，慕容仁鎮平郭。

translations.literal: Hui moved Murong Han to garrison Liaodong and Murong Ren to garrison Pingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Hui posted Murong Han at Liaodong and Murong Ren at Pingguo.

sentences.zh: 翰撫安民夷，甚有威惠；

translations.literal: Han pacified and comforted Han Chinese and Yi barbarians, possessing much authority and kindness;
translations.idiomatic: Han governed Chinese and tribal peoples alike with stern authority and humane care;

sentences.zh: 仁亦次之。

translations.literal: Ren also ranked next.
translations.idiomatic: Ren was nearly as capable.

sentences.zh: 拓跋猗□妻惟氏，忌代王鬱律之強，恐不利於其子，乃殺鬱律而立其子賀人辱，大人死者數十人。

translations.literal: Tuoba Yilu□'s wife Lady Wei, jealous of Prince of Dai Yulu's strength, fearing it would not benefit her son, therefore killed Yulu and established her son Herenru as ruler; several tens of great men died.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wei, wife of Tuoba Yilu, resented the Prince of Dai Yulu's power and feared it threatened her son. She had Yulu killed and installed her son Herenru as ruler, and several dozen tribal chieftains died in the bloodbath.

sentences.zh: 鬱律之子什翼犍，幼在襁褓，其母王氏匿於褲中，祝之曰：「天苟存汝，則勿啼。」

translations.literal: Yulu's son Shiyijian, still an infant in swaddling clothes, his mother Lady Wang hid him in trousers, praying to him: 'If Heaven would preserve you, then do not cry.
translations.idiomatic: Yulu's infant son Shiyijian was hidden by his mother, Lady Wang, inside a pair of trousers. She whispered a prayer: 'If Heaven means to save you, do not cry.

sentences.zh: 久之，不啼，乃得免。

translations.literal: After long time he did not cry, and thereby was spared.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he did not cry, and so survived.

sentences.zh: 惟氏專制國政，遣使聘後趙，後趙人謂之「女國使」。

translations.literal: Lady Wei monopolized control of state affairs, dispatched envoys to pay court to Later Zhao—Later Zhao people called them 'envoys of the woman's state.'
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wei dominated the government and sent envoys to Later Zhao, which the Later Zhao court dubbed the 'envoys from the kingdom of women.'
